description:
The Town and the Fort Myers Beach Fire Control District share responsibility for enforcing the Florida Fire Prevention Code, Chapter 633, Florida Statutes, and local fire prevention ordinances. The Town does not employ a Fire Official, Fire Marshal, or Fire Safety Inspector and relies on the District to fill these roles. The Fire Control and Prevention Interlocal Agreement dated December 18, 2013 has expired by its own terms.
The MOU replaces the 2013 agreement in its entirety. It designates the District's Fire Chief as Fire Official for the Town, requires the District to provide a Fire Safety Inspector, and allows the Town Manager to appoint the Fire Chief and designees as Code Inspectors for the limited purpose of enforcing the Fire Code. Exhibit A divides development review, plan review, permitting, and inspection duties, including a permit responsibility matrix. The Town retains residential permits and residential fuel gas systems, and the District handles commercial fire plan review and commercial fuel gas permits. The MOU has a five-year term, may be renewed for five years by mutual written consent, and may be canceled by either party on thirty days' written notice. It does not affect the separate agreement for use of Town hall chambers and hydrant maintenance.

description: On August 4, 2025, the Town Council awarded the Water Meter Replacement Program (ITB-25-05-PW) to National Metering Services, Inc. through Resolution 25-235, and the Agreement was signed August 19, 2025. The First Amendment (November 3, 2025, Resolution 25-299) changed the meter technology for the 5/8-inch and 1-inch meters and antennas from a radio frequency (RF) model to a cellular model, which provides 99.9% island coverage compared to approximately 90% for RF. It increased the cost by $204,162, setting the not-to-exceed amount at $1,823,952. The Second Amendment (February 2, 2026, Resolution 26-038) added sub-foot-accuracy GPS geospatial data points and a Lead and Copper Service Line Identification Inventory for all meters in the distribution system. It added $96,900, setting the not-to-exceed amount at $1,920,852. The Third Amendment (June 15, 2026, Resolution 26-126) expanded the scope to include replacement of the 1½, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6-inch water meters and associated costs, setting the total not-to-exceed amount at $2,446,761. The Fourth Amendment extends the time for completion by six months, to April 20, 2027, with no increase in the not-to-exceed amount.

description:

Only the following individuals will be present and allowed to participate during the Executive Session: Mayor Dan Allers, Vice-Mayor Scott Safford, Council Members John R. description:
Per Town of Fort Myers Beach Code of Ordinances, Division 3.—Local Planning Agency (LPA)
Sec. 34-112. - Purpose and Scope.
The broad objectives of town planning and the creation of the local planning agency are to further the welfare of the citizens of the town by helping to promote a better, more helpful, convenient, efficient, healthful, safe, and attractive community environment and to insure that the unique and natural characteristics of the island are preserved.
Sec. 34-113. - Composition, appointment and compensation of members.(a)The local planning agency shall consist of up to seven members appointed by the town council. No members of the local planning agency shall be salaried officials of the town. Membership on the local planning agency shall not affect a person's eligibility for membership on any other advisory committee for the Town of Fort Myers Beach during his/her term of office. One spouse per household will be eligible for membership on the local planning agency during any given term of office. No current member of town council shall be eligible to serve on the local planning agency. Except for inclusion of members required under Florida law, all members must be registered voters within the territorial boundaries of the Town of Fort Myers Beach at the time of application for membership on the local planning agency and during the period of service on the local planning agency. All applicants must apply on or before October 1 of the appointment year. Each application must include a short biography and short explanation as to why the applicant wishes to serve on the local planning agency.
(b)The members of the local planning agency shall serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for expenses as are necessary to conduct the work of the agency from funds appropriated by the town council.
(c)In addition to the up to seven voting members, the local planning agency shall also include as a nonvoting member a representative of the Lee County School District, as designated by the Lee County School Board, to attend and participate in those meetings at which the local planning agency considers comprehensive plan amendments and rezonings that would, if approved, increase residential density on the property that is the subject of the application (see F.S. 163.3174(1), 2002).
(d)All appointed members of the local planning agency must file an annual financial disclosure as required by the Florida Commission on Ethics.

description:
The Neighborhood Company, on behalf of SLASA LLC, is requesting rezoning of the property located at 5601 and 5607 Estero Boulevard from the Commercial Resort (CR) zoning district to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) for redevelopment of the historic Hideaway Village Model. The subject property is located on the north-east side of Estero Boulevard at Lazy Way and Lewis Street. The property consists of approximately 0.63 acres and is identified as STRAP(s) #33-46-24-W2-00204.0290 and 33-46-24-W2-00001.0120. Before Hurricane Ian, the property contained the Hideaway Village Motel, a three-building, two-story lodging development with 23 total units, including 22 guest units, together with a swimming pool, outdoor dining areas, and on and off-site parking.
The applicant proposes a CPD rezoning to allow redevelopment of the site with a 30-unit boutique hotel and complementary restaurant, café/coffee shop, limited accessory retail, and hotel amenities.
The proposed Master Concept Plan includes 30 lodging units, up to 3,500 square feet of restaurant and commercial space, a minimum of 36 parking spaces.
The Master Concept plan relocates most parking beneath or behind the principal structure, eliminates direct vehicular access and backing movements onto Estero Boulevard, provides ingress from Lazy Way and egress to Lewis Street, adds a sidewalk along Lazy Way, and incorporates enhanced landscaping and pedestrian amenities along Estero Boulevard and Lazy Way. Five parking spaces are proposed within Lewis Street right-of-way and would require separate authorization under the Town’s private use-of-right-of-way process.
On September 8, 2026, LPA voted unanimously (6-0) to recommend approval with conditions for a CPD amendment request with 9 deviations, CPD 20260039, to rezone the property, Commercial Resort (CR) to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) to redevelop Hideaway Village with 30 boutique hotel unit and 3,500 square feet of commercial space.

description:
DiamondHead Beach Resort, through its agent The Neighborhood Company, requests approval of a Commercial Planned Development (CPD) rezoning for approximately 3.45 acres located at 1999 and 2000 Estero Boulevard approximately 2.38 acres (revised September 9/15/2026) within the Times Square Mixed-Use/Pedestrian Commercial area as the CPD area. The request would recognize existing resort, incorporate the existing parking parcel north of Estero Boulevard, and allow redevelopment and expansion of the existing resort.
The DiamondHead Beach Resort was originally approved by Lee County through Development Order (DO) No. 94-12-024, prior to the incorporation of the Town of Fort Myers Beach. According to the applicant, the original Development Order approved 154 resort units in two phases. Phase I, consisting of approximately 124 resort units and associated amenities, was constructed. Phase II authorized 30 additional resort units and a parking structure. In 2018, three hotel units were removed to accommodate construction of the Coste Island Cuisine restaurant. Staff understand that 121 hotel rooms currently exist while the construction of the restaurant accounted for the 3 unbuilt units from first phase. “Thus, according to the applicant, 30 previously approved hotel units remain unbuilt.
The CPD application proposes 57 additional hotel rooms, consisting of 30 rooms claimed as vested and 27 rooms beyond the vested entitlement. resulting in a total of 178 hotel rooms in DiamondHead Resort. The revised CPD application proposes 55 additional hotel rooms consisting of 30 unbuilt rooms and 25 additional rooms beyond the vested entitlement, resulting in a maximum of 176 hotel rooms. The applicant submitted supporting documentation including correspondence, project process sheets, and prior approval records indicating approval of the original Development Order and subsequent amendments. The application also incorporates the existing parking parcel located at 1999 Estero Boulevard, which has historically operated under Special Exception Resolution 03-11 for employees and overflow guest parking. The applicant acknowledges that approval of the proposed CPD would supersede and vacate the existing Special Exception.
No amendment to the Future Land Use category has been submitted with this application. The revised September 2026 MCP states that the ±1.07-acre Recreation and Open Space/Environmentally Critical area is outside the ±2.38-acre CPD area.
Proposed Development
The revised Master Concept Plan proposes:
Expansion of the existing resort from 121 existing hotel rooms to a maximum of 178 hotel rooms;
Revised narrative and MPC Expansion of the existing resort from 121 existing hotel rooms to a maximum of 176 hotel rooms;
Recognition of the previously approved 30 vested hotel units together with 27 (24 new + 3) 30 unbuilt hotel units together with 25 additional rooms;
The Existing Restaurant Location Exhibit identifies approximately 1,870 square feet for the existing Cabanas Beach Bar & Grill and approximately 4,825 square feet for Coste Island Cuisine.
Approximately 1,600 square feet of outdoor beach-area seating.
Improvements to the existing parking facilities on both the primary resort parcel and the parking parcel north of Estero Boulevard;
Continued use of existing access points from Estero Boulevard with no new vehicular access proposed; and
Pedestrian connections between the north parking parcel and the main resort property.
On September 8th, 2006, the LPA unanimously (6-0) recommended denial of CPD 202600099 with as presented. The recommendation was based primarily on the proposed 24-unit beachside building and the insufficiency of the identified public benefits to justify its requested height, intensity, and compatibility impacts. The LPA generally supported the 33-unit addition to the existing resort building but did not support the scale and location of the separate beachside building.

description:
James Ink, with Ink Engineering Inc., the registered applicant on behalf of property owner Calusa, LLC, is requesting rezoning of 0.19+/- acres of the 0.44-acre total lot area, including 0.25 acres in the EC zoning district, from Residential Multifamily (RM) to Residential Planned Development (RPD), with a Master Concept Plan, seven (7) deviations, and a lot-line adjustment.
The two subject properties are part of property originally platted as Lot 17, Unit 3, Island Shores, as recorded on April 16, 1951, in Plat Book 9, Page 27, of the official records of Lee County, Florida. This parcel was 100 feet wide and extended from Estero Blvd. to the mean high-water line of the Gulf of Mexico. The property was subsequently subdivided again in 1992 in Official Record Book 2327 Page 1442. This created the subject parcels and was done before incorporation of the Town of Fort Myers Beach on December 31, 1995. The subject properties were in existence before the incorporation of the town therefore the two dwelling units that existed before Hurricane Ian were legal and conforming with zoning code at time of creation.
Based on pre-storm (Hurricane Ian) data from Lee Property Appraiser (LEEPA) and ariel imagery available, each lot contained one dwelling unit of approximately 800 square feet built in 1951 (584 Estero Blvd.) and 1965 (582 Estero Blvd) respectively. The existing lot area for each site are 2557 square feet (582 Estero blvd) and 538 square feet (including EC zone for 584 Estero Blvd).
The applicant requests deviations from the underlying RM zoning district standards related to minimum lot area, setbacks, and maximum lot coverage to facilitate redevelopment and a proposed lot line adjustment. While dimensional relief for nonconforming lots is typically addressed through the variance process, the proposed lot line adjustment would reduce the area of the larger parcel at 582 Estero Boulevard while increasing the area of the smaller parcel at 584 Estero Boulevard. Because a variance cannot be used to increase the degree of nonconformity of an existing lot, the requested lot line adjustment cannot be accomplished through a variance. The proposed project will be constructed in two phases.
On August 11, 2026, LPA voted unanimously (5-0) to recommend approval with conditions for RPD amendment request with 7 deviations, RPD 20260529, to rezone the property from Residential Multifamily (RM) to Residential Planned Development to permit reconstruction of two single-family residences with a lot-line adjustment.
On September 9, 2026, Town Council voted unanimously (4-0) to recommend approval with conditions for RPD amendment request with 7 deviations, RPD 20260529, to rezone the property from Residential Multifamily (RM) to Residential Planned Development to permit reconstruction of two single-family residences with a lot-line adjustment.

description:
On April 20, 2026, the Town Council approved Resolution No. 26-078, awarding ITB-26-05-EN and authorizing an Independent Contractor's Agreement with Earth Tech Enterprises, Inc. for the purchase, transport, delivery, and placement of beach compatible sand to restore scour holes and rebuild emergency berms along Estero Island. The Agreement estimated a fill quantity of approximately 60,400 tons at a not-to-exceed amount of $2,099,100.00, with a performance period of fifty-five (55) days from the date of Notice to Proceed.
Based on updated survey and field conditions, the Town's engineer of record determined that additional sand was necessary to complete the restoration consistent with the Town's engineered beach design. On June 15, 2026, a walk-on item was presented to the Town Council proposing a First Amendment increasing the estimated quantity to 68,400 tons and the not-to-exceed amount by $272,000.00, and the Council authorized the Town Manager to negotiate and execute the First Amendment on behalf of the Town.
Following that authorization, the engineer of record further revised the required quantity based on updated survey data to an estimated 70,800 tons, an increase of 10,400 tons over the original quantity, resulting in an increase of $353,600.00 at the Agreement unit prices of $28.00 per ton for delivery and $6.00 per ton for placement. The additional quantity also required additional time for performance, and the original fifty-five (55) day performance period was superseded by a contract completion deadline of December 31, 2026. The Town Manager signed the First Amendment on June 24, 2026 under the authority granted by Council and is now seeking ratification.

description:
The Town's property & casualty coverage is provided through the Florida Municipal Insurance Trust (FMIT), Policy FMIT 0778, covering General/Professional Liability, Cyber Liability, Automobile Liability, Automobile Physical Damage, Property, and Workers' Compensation.
FMIT's original renewal quote for 2026-2027 reflected an overall increase of 11.0%, bringing the Town's total net premium to $1,624,926. Through negotiation, the Human Resources Director worked with FMIT to reduce the renewal increase to 9.0%, lowering the total net premium to $1,586,216, a savings of $38,710 to the Town. The reduction was driven by lower premiums on the Automobile Liability, Automobile Physical Damage, and Property lines; General/Professional Liability, Cyber Liability, and Workers' Compensation premiums were unchanged between the two quotes.
After a comprehensive review, Human Resources, through the Town Manager, recommends that the Town accept the negotiated renewal at the 9.0% increase to capture this savings while maintaining full coverage across all lines.
This item is being presented at this time to ensure the Town has uninterrupted property & casualty coverage effective October 1, 2026. Final terms remain subject to execution of the FMIT renewal agreement.

description:
On August 21, 2026, the Town entered into a cooperative purchase (piggyback) agreement with Doosan Bobcat North America, Inc. under Sourcewell Contract #020223-CEC for medium duty and compact construction equipment, related attachments, and associated parts and services. The agreement was executed administratively with a not-to-exceed amount of $62,875.05, which was below the threshold requiring Council approval.
The Town has identified additional equipment, attachment, and parts needs for the remainder of Fiscal Year 2026 and for Fiscal Year 2027. The proposed First Amendment increases the aggregate not-to-exceed amount to $90,000.00 for the remaining term of the agreement, coterminous with the Sourcewell contract. Because the amended amount exceeds the Town Manager's authority, Council approval is required. The finance department director has determined that continued purchasing under the Sourcewell contract at the increased amount remains financially advantageous to the Town. All purchases remain contingent upon appropriation.

description: On December 15, 2025, the Town entered into an Independent Contractor's Agreement with TideWater Landscape of Florida, LLC, following the competitive solicitation of RFP-26-01-PW, Fort Myers Beach Landscaping and Irrigation, for landscaping and irrigation repairs to residential and community areas damaged or disturbed by utility work. The Agreement is a three-year, unit-price agreement under which all work is authorized in writing through Supplemental Task Authorizations. Exhibit "B" (Compensation and Pricing) as executed contains two separate unit-price schedules for the same materials - one excluding labor and one including labor - which has created ambiguity in the pricing and review of Contractor invoices. The proposed First Amendment amends and restates Exhibit "B" in its entirety to delete the material-only schedule and consolidate all materials into a single schedule inclusive of labor, and to add eleven additional unit-price items not contemplated at the time of award.

description:
The Neighborhood Company, on behalf of FMBH, LLC, is requesting approval of a Development Agreement with deviations for the redevelopment of the former Wyndham/Holiday Inn property located at 6890 Estero Boulevard. The proposal includes a phased redevelopment consisting of a restaurant, open-air entertainment venue, recreational uses, accessory parking, and future joint parking operations.
Phase 1: Open a restaurant and entertainment venue with recreational uses as quickly as possible. To expedite the opening of the venue, temporary mobile vending trailers will be utilized to comply with FEMA and Florida Building Code flood regulations.
Phase 2: This phase will require the design, permitting, and construction of a wave-dissipation wall, combined with a flood map revision to change the property's flood zone from VE to AE. The map change will allow for the construction of permanent, dry-floodproofed structures that will replace and eliminate the use of temporary trailers. Additionally, the recreational uses will be expanded to include a pool and lazy river. The two phases are described in greater detail below.
The underlying zoning for the property is Commercial Resort (CR), which has housed hotels, including the Holiday Inn and Wyndham Garden, since 1969. The property was severely damaged during Hurricane Ian in 2022. The property owner believes that the highest and best use for the property was, and remains, a resort hotel. However, current financial conditions remain unfavorable for establishing a resort hotel. As a result, the Development Agreement will allow the limited uses outlined in Phases 1 and 2, as depicted in Exhibits C and D of the agreement. The agreement also includes permitted uses under the current CR zoning district, including Commercial Resort uses; however, those uses cannot be developed or constructed unless the Development Agreement is amended or terminated.
On June 16, 2026, the Local Planning Agency (LPA) voted 6-1 to recommend approval with conditions of Development Agreement request DA20250277, including seven deviations, to allow the redevelopment of a restaurant and family entertainment venue on the former Wyndham/Holiday Inn property. The request proposes phased development. The LPA recommended that the following conditions be incorporated into the Development Agreement:
Include a defined timeline for completion of Phase 1 in the Development Agreement.
Require both ingress and egress access points to include paved driveway aprons.
Require a parking attendant to be present on-site during all operating hours.
Require public restrooms to remain locked when the facility is closed and outside of operating hours.
Require the applicant to evaluate alternative landscaping enhancements, including larger landscape planters, where feasible and subject to approval by the Town Engineer.
Require submission of an updated traffic impact analysis as part of the Phase 2 Development Order application.
Add the Lee County Department of Transportation to the list of required governmental agencies from which permits or approvals must be obtained prior to development.
On August 3, 2026, the Town Council unanimously voted to recommend approval with conditions of Development Agreement request DA20250277, including seven deviations, to allow the redevelopment of a restaurant and family entertainment venue on the former Wyndham/Holiday Inn property. The Town Council recommended that the following conditions be incorporated into the Development Agreement:
Additional Signage:Educational signage regarding the Environmentally Critical Area.
Signage requiring all dogs to be on a leash.
No camper parking / no overnight parking signage.
Temporary Units:Require all temporary units to comply with the Town's floodplain regulations.
Ingress/Egress:Require both access points to provide ingress and egress.
Temporary Certificate of Occupancy:Address the issuance of a "Temporary CO" and establish a timeframe for the applicant to explain any delay if Phase 2 does not begin within five years.

description:
The Neighborhood Company, on behalf of TPI-FMB Suites LLC, is requesting rezoning of the property located at 1207 Estero Boulevard from the Downtown zoning district to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) for redevelopment of the historic Silver Sands Resort. The property consists of approximately 0.74 acres and is identified as STRAP #19-46-24-W4-0150D.0050. The Future Land Use designation is Times Square Mixed-use Commercial, and the property is located within the Downtown zoning district.
The proposed application includes a new Master Concept Plan (MCP) for the site consisting of:
A 60-unit boutique-style hotel
Approximately 2,500 square feet of ground-floor commercial space,
51 on-site parking spaces,
Rooftop pool and amenity deck,
Canal-side activation area and dock improvements,
Streetscape and pedestrian improvements along Estero Boulevard and Primo Drive.
The proposed maximum building height will be approximately 58 feet as measured from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Lowest Horizontal Structural Member (LHSM), with an overall building height of approximately 70 feet from grade to the roof peak. The building will consist of six stories, including a ground-level parking floor. The maximum height will be limited to the center of the building and that the majority of the structure, front and rear, will be stepped down and limited to 5 stories.
On June 16, 2026, the LPA voted unanimously (7-0) to recommend approval with conditions for CPD 20250286, including 11 deviations, to rezone the property from Downtown to Commercial Planned Development for the redevelopment of Silver Sands Resort.
On August 3, 2026, the Town Council voted unanimously (4-0) to approve on first reading, with conditions, CPD 20250286, including 10 deviations, to rezone the property from the Downtown zoning district to Commercial Planned Development for the development of Silver Sands Resort/One Particular Harbour.
In response to the Town Council’s direction, the applicant submitted revised materials dated August 15, 2026, incorporating the following changes:
Master Concept Plan:Relocated the dumpster.
Removed the sidewalk along the northern property line along Primo Drive.
Added a five-foot right-of-way easement along Primo Drive.
Removed the canal-side COP area.
Relocated and updated the deviation triangles.
Removed two parking spaces on Primo Drive and added parking under the building.
Request Narrative:Updated for consistency with the revised plans.
Schedule of Deviations and Justifications:Removed the northern buffer-width deviation.
Removed the Primo Drive sidewalk-width deviation.
Revised the signage deviation and added a deviation for the proposed wayfinding pole sign
Revised the refuse-container-screening deviation.
Reduced the requested parking-deviation percentage.
Vehicle-Stacking Exhibit:Updated to reflect the revised layout presented at the first Town Council meeting.

description:
The Town does not independently operate an animal control program and currently contracts with Lee County, through its Domestic Animal Services division, for stray animal control services including field response, sheltering, adoption, and related services. Lee County has prepared a proposed Five-Year Interlocal Agreement covering the period of October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2031. Under the Agreement, the Town's annual fee is based on the County's actual net expenses for the corresponding fiscal year, and the Town also compensates the County for Capital Improvement Projects based on the Town's proportionate share of stray animals impounded by jurisdiction. By correspondence dated June 4, 2026, Lee County advised that the charge for Fiscal Year 2026-2027 will be $7,087.00.
In response to the Town's follow-up inquiries, Lee County Domestic Animal Services confirmed that the County is not currently anticipating upgrading or constructing a new shelter, and identified the City of Bonita Springs, the Village of Estero, the City of Fort Myers, and the City of Cape Coral as the other municipalities participating in similar interlocal agreements. Either party may terminate the Agreement upon sixty (60) days' written notice.

description:
The Town of Fort Myers Beach (the "Town") seeks qualifications from professional engineering and architectural firms to provide comprehensive design, permitting, and construction-phase engineering and inspection (CEI) services for the North Island Water Tower Replacement project. This project, funded in part through Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) funds, aims to restore and modernize the North Island potable water storage and pump station infrastructure severely impacted by Hurricane Ian. The firm selected will provide professional services for the Public Facilities Infrastructure Program.
Pursuant to Sec. 2-480(h)(1) of the Town's Code of Ordinances and the Consultant's Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA), contracts for professional services consisting of Professional Engineering or Registered Land Surveying must be competitively negotiated in accordance with the requirements of Section 287.055 F.S. within statutory thresholds. In addition, the Town competitively bids for other professional services as further described below.
The Town solicited this project under RFQ-26-03-AD, with Tetra Tech, INC. determined to be the most qualified respondent through the competitive qualifications review process.
In accordance with the Town of Fort Myers Beach Purchasing Ordinance 26-06, Sec 2-480(14) the Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) consisting of a minimum of three members, may be established for the purpose of evaluating bids submitted to the Town. All members of the SAC are prohibited from speaking, answering questions or having contact with any potential bidder. The SAC will review the bid and response materials prior to the SAC meeting. The committee evaluates each firm's qualifications based on past experience, express understanding of the project and proposed method of handling the project and any other criteria included for evaluation.
The Town's SAC evaluated the qualifications submittals received in response to RFQ-26-03-AD and, at a noticed public meeting, publicly evaluated each firm based upon the established criteria within the Request for Qualifications document. The SAC ranked Tetra Tech, INC. as the most responsive and qualified firm and forwarded this recommendation to the Town Manager. The Town Manager, after reviewing the SAC recommendation, forwarded this to the Town Council for consideration during a regularly scheduled meeting. The Town Council reviewed the rankings and qualifications of the firms and voted to accept the rankings by the Town Manager. The Town Council also directed the Town Manager or designee to initiate negotiations with the top-ranked firm, Tetra Tech, INC.
Following negotiations and Lee County approval of the draft agreement, the Agreement for Fort Myers Beach Engineering & Architectural Services - North Island Water Tower (Contract No. 26-03-AD) is now going before the Town Council for final approval. The Agreement provides for Phase 1 professional services in an amount not to exceed $1,124,792, with Phase 2 not to exceed $739,865 if subsequently authorized by the Town in writing upon completion of Phase 1.

description:
The Town has been involved with a long-standing island-wide street lighting project to address streetlights across the island. The current Statement of Work provides for the installation of lighting along Estero Boulevard, the Town side streets, and the Downtown area. The project remains on target and is expected to be completed early next year.
During the 2023 Legislative Session, the Florida Legislature appropriated $350,000,000 for the Hurricane Ian and Nicole Grant Recovery Program to help local governments mitigate local and county revenue losses and operating deficits; make infrastructure repairs and replacements including road, sewer, and water facilities; conduct beach nourishment; and complete debris removal. On November 7, 2023, the Lee County Board of County Commissioners accepted an award from the Florida Division of Emergency Management that included a grant sub-award of $7,766,387 to the Town as a sub-recipient, with Lee County acting as pass-through entity, for the installation of sea turtle lighting on Estero Boulevard and its side streets. The Florida Division of Emergency Management and Lee County subsequently agreed to amend the Grant Agreement so that the award would be made directly to the Town, eliminating Lee County as the pass-through entity.
The Town entered into its Agreement with FPL Energy Services, Inc. in November 2023, and the parties executed Amendment No. 1 effective April 20, 2026. Amendment No. 2 accomplishes two things. First, it revises the Lighting Scope of Equipment to reflect the adjusted quantities actually used as compared to the permitted quantities. This allows FPL Energy Services and its subcontractor to provide the Town, upon completion, with an actual count of the poles and fixtures used along with a detailed map of the exact locations where they were installed. Second, wire previously installed at the site was stolen and must be replaced to complete the project. FPL Energy Services will facilitate the replacement, including the purchase and installation of an estimated 54,000 linear feet of wire, at a cost not to exceed $150,000. Those funds are made available by reducing the ten-year maintenance amount from $300,000 to $150,000, so there is no increase to the not-to-exceed Implementation Price. Any unspent portion is returned to the maintenance amount by subsequent amendment following final inspection, supported by detailed invoices, quantities, unit costs, installation records, and testing documentation acceptable to the Town.
The investigation into the thefts remains ongoing. The replacement work and funding arrangement are a cooperative measure to keep the project on schedule and do not allocate or determine responsibility for the thefts. Neither party admits fault or liability, and both parties reserve all claims, defenses, rights, and remedies.

FOR THE ISLAND-WIDE STREET LIGHTING PROJECT; REVISING THE LIGHTING SCOPE OF EQUIPMENT TO REFLECT ADJUSTED QUANTITIES; PROVIDING FOR A REVISED DESIGN DRAWING; REALLOCATING ONE HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($150,000.00) FROM THE MAINTENANCE SERVICE TERM AMOUNT TO FUND THE REPLACEMENT OF STOLEN WIRE, WITH NO ADMISSION OF FAULT OR LIABILITY BY EITHER PARTY AND WITH ALL CLAIMS, DEFENSES, RIGHTS, AND REMEDIES RESERVED; PROVIDING FOR NO INCREASE TO THE NOT-TO-EXCEED IMPLEMENTATION PRICE OF $7,766,387.00; AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE THE AMENDMENT; PROVIDING FOR SEVERABILITY; AND PROVIDING FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE.

attachments.name: Final NS 26-204 Increase Purchasing Capabilities for the Meters and Supplies From Ferguson Enterprises 1

description:
Ferguson Enterprises is the sole supplier in the State of Florida for Neptune metering supplies. The Neptune metering system is the system the Town uses for all water usage monitoring and for billing customers based on usage data.
In accordance with the Town's Purchasing Ordinance (Ordinance 26-06, Section 2-480(c)), when total purchases from a sole supplier (or any single vendor) exceed $75,000 within a fiscal year, Council approval is required to continue purchasing from that vendor. Staff is requesting an increased NTE amount of $20,000 for the remainder of Fiscal Year 2026 and $100,000 for Fiscal Year 2027.
The Town is currently undertaking an island-wide meter change-out program. Throughout the year, additional needs also arise within that program: properties are split, customers request larger meters, developments are rebuilt and require upsized meters, or a change in property use requires a different meter type along with its associated supplies. The Town must be able to respond to these requests as they arise to support an efficient project schedule and a growing community.

description:
On May 3, 2022, the Town entered into a Government Agency Agreement and Order Form with Flock Group, Inc. for automated license plate recognition (ALPR) cameras and access to Flock's software platform. The Order Form provided for an initial term of twenty-four (24) months with successive renewal terms and a deployment of six (6) Flock Falcon Cameras at $2,500.00 per camera annually, for a recurring annual amount of $15,000.00, plus a one-time implementation fee of $1,500.00 (Year 1 total of $16,500.00). Section 6.2 of the Agreement allows the Town to self-elect termination for convenience at any time during the term, effective immediately upon Flock's receipt of notice. Termination results in a one-time fee of $500.00 per Falcon Camera - $3,000.00 for the Town's six cameras - and entitles the Town to a refund for the Falcon Cameras prorated for any fees covering the remaining term. Flock is responsible for removing all Flock Hardware within a commercially reasonable period following termination.

description:
The Citizen of Distinction Award is designed to recognize, on an annual basis, an outstanding citizen who has made an exceptional contribution to our Town.
The Town received four nominations this year: three in the Arts and Culture category and one in the Beach Heritage category. The submission deadline was extended by Town Council to late June.
Arts and Culture: The Town of Fort Myers Beach recognizes citizens, groups, or organizations that have distinguished themselves through an artistic or cultural project. Nominees may be current or former residents and must have resided full- or part-time on Fort Myers Beach for at least three years. Businesses or groups must have been operating within the Town for at least three years.
Beach Heritage: This award is given to a citizen or citizens who have contributed significantly to the heritage of Fort Myers Beach. The recipient(s) must be a full-time resident of Fort Myers Beach.
The nominees for 2026 in the Arts and Culture category are:
Christine Begy, President & CEO, Wonderful Creations 777 Inc. – Nominated for Frederick, the Majestic Egret in Lilies! Nominated by Christine Begy, President & CEO, Wonderful Creations 777 Inc.
Rosemary Bishton – Nominated for her beautification project on North Estero Boulevard following Hurricanes Ian, Helene, and Milton. Nominated by Dr. John Renaldo, OD.
Dawn Miller, Founder & President, What's Up FMB – Nominated for her outstanding leadership and dedication to bringing residents, visitors, and local businesses together while helping revitalize Fort Myers Beach and strengthen its sense of community following Hurricane Ian..
The nominees for 2026 in the Beach Heritage category are: Joy and Kevin Sullivan – Nominated for their longstanding leadership, volunteerism, environmental advocacy, philanthropy, and dedication to strengthening and preserving the Fort Myers Beach community.
The selected recipient(s) will be formally recognized at the Thursday, November 5, 2026Town Council meeting. In the past, the Citizen of Distinction has also been honored as the Grand Marshal of the Town's annual Fourth of July Parade. If the Council wishes to continue this tradition, a selection needs to be made.
Note: the Mangrove Tree that was located in Town Hall Council Chambers, which has traditionally displayed engraved leaves recognizing Citizen of Distinction recipients, sustained severe damage during Hurricane Ian. The Town is currently exploring options for either replacing the tree or creating a new way to memorialize recipients.
title: Select the recipient(s) of the 2026 Citizen of Distinction Award from the four nominations received, and provide direction to staff for the Grand Marshal recognition in the Town’s annual Fourth of July Parade.

attachments.name: Form 8B - Safford - Town Atty Item A 8.3.26

description:
ROAR Offshore Powerboat Races LLC has submitted a Special Event Application for the 2026 return of the ROAR Offshore Powerboat Races, to be held September 11 through September 13, 2026. Event operations and emergency support will be based at Margaritaville Beach Resort and associated properties, with racing activities taking place directly offshore. The application and supporting materials identify an expected attendance of approximately 5,000 to 12,000 people. Supporting site plans identify 18 planned vessel placements across multiple staging locations associated with the event.
The event requires Town Council approval for the requested ordinance waivers and use of waterways within the Town’s jurisdiction. The applicant is also proposing a boat show within Times Square, with five race teams displaying vessels approximately 32 feet in length. The applicant is also requesting the rental of 22 Town parking spaces at Beach Access 36 (Wastina Way) to support the staging of additional vessels. The Whale property will also provide support and vessel staging as part of the event footprint.
Race boats will be lowered into and removed from the water by crane at the designated crane and wash-down support site on the One Particular Harbor site across from the Whale at 1207 Estero Blvd. The supporting staging plan identifies this area as a temporary operational site where boats will be staged only during scheduled launch and retrieval operations.
As of the preparation of this Blue Sheet, the Special Event Application remains partially incomplete. Final approvals from a full review by staff, the Fort Myers Beach Fire Control District and Lee County Sheriff’s Office remain outstanding, along with proof of insurance as required by the Town’s Special Event permitting process.
title:
Approval of the ROAR Offshore 2026 Powerboat Races Special Event, to be held September 11 through September 13, 2026, at and offshore of Margaritaville Beach Resort, as requested by ROAR Offshore Powerboat Races LLC, including authorization for the waiver of enforcement of the Town’s noise and open container ordinances; use of waterways within the Town’s jurisdiction; use of applicable Town beach property; use of Town property; subject to final approval by the Fort Myers Beach Fire Control District, Lee County Sheriff’s Office, and Town staff.
Additional information will be provided at beginning of the meeting.

attachments.name: 26-177, Advisory Committees Policies and Procedures Manual

description:
The proposed Advisory Committee Policies and Procedures Manual was developed to establish a consistent administrative and procedural framework for the Town’s advisory committees, boards, and agencies. The Manual provides guidance regarding roles and responsibilities, meeting procedures, attendance, professional conduct, Sunshine Law and public records requirements, communication and representation, reporting procedures, and other operational expectations.
The Manual was presented to the Town Council during the August 6, 2026, Management & Planning meeting, at which time Council provided feedback and direction. The Manual has been updated to incorporate that feedback.
The Manual is intended to promote consistency, transparency, accountability, legal and policy compliance, and effective communication among Advisory Committee members, Town Council, Council Liaisons, Staff Liaisons, the Town Clerk’s Office, and Town Administration. Adoption of the Manual will provide a centralized resource for Advisory Committee members and Town staff while preserving the individual duties and responsibilities assigned to each committee by applicable law, ordinance, resolution, or other governing authority.

attachments.name: Resolution 26-172 - ADOPTING AN UPDATED COMPREHENSIVE EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT PLAN
CEMP 2026 Draft Policy - For Council Approval

description:
The Town CEMP (Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan) establishes uniform policies and procedures consistent with NIMS for the effective coordination of resources to cope with a wide variety of natural, man-made, and technological emergencies. These emergencies may differ in size and severity and might affect the health, safety, or general welfare of the people of the Town of Fort Myers Beach.
Pursuant to F.A.C. 27P-6.010, (8), this plan,shall be adopted by resolution of the governing body of the jurisdiction before it becomes the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan for such local government. Modifications to the plan made between formal approvals by the governing body that are not substantive shall be considered administrative updates to the previously approved plan and do not require approval of the governing body, but must be approved by the Town Manager.
Plan Distribution
The Town of Fort Myers Beach CEMP will be comprehensively reviewed once every four years,or whenever significant revisions are necessary, or as directed by the Town Manager. The plan will be distributed to the following individuals for input:
 Town Manager
 All Town Department Directors
 Lee County Emergency Management Division Chief
 Lee County Sheriff’s Office
 Fire Chief, Fort Myers Beach Fire Control District
 Town Building Official
When adopted,the Plan shall be placed on the Town's website and distributed to the persons listed above and to the Town Clerk.
In addition, the Town Manager will periodically review emergency management assignments within the Emergency Operations Center with the goal of developing each position to a depth of two levels for each vital position. Individuals assigned to the roster will be notified of any updates to the Plan.This shall include:
 Mayor and Town Council
 Incident Command
 Planning Section Chief
 Logistics Section Chief
 Operations Section Chief
 Finance Administration Section Chief
 Public Information Officer
 Fire Chief
 Sheriff
 Emergency Management Coordinator
It shall be their responsibility to read and review the plan and be fully aware of the role they play in an emergency, and to disseminate it to and review it with appropriate members of their staff.

attachments.name: NS 26-175, Health Insurance Renewal Resolution FINAL (1)

description:
The Town’s current medical coverage is provided through Cigna while dental, vision, life, STD, & LTD is through the Standard. The current increase from Cigna for medical coverage represents 11% or $140,986. Should the Town elect to switch providers for dental & vision insurance coverage to Cigna, Cigna offered a 1.1% discount on the overall increase down to 9.9% or $126, 903 which is a net savings of 1.1% or $14,083. Additionally, transferring vision coverage through Cigna would see a 1.7% reduction or $123.00 in annual premium ($7,022 annually) and dental coverage would renew flat with no increase ($51,708 annually).
After a comprehensive review, Human Resources, through the Town Manager, recommends that the Town renew the medical coverage with Cigna and transfer dental and vision coverage from The Standard to Cigna to capture this savings and improve employee experience and access to care.
This item is being presented at this time to allow the Town to hold open enrollment in September and ensure employees have uninterrupted access to care effective October 1, 2026. Final plan structure, coverage, and rates remain subject to final budget adoption and may change.

attachments.name: 26-173, Acceptance of Sand Donation from Millworth Group

description:
The Town recognizes the benefit of private donations from individuals, community groups, and businesses to fund new and existing facilities, services, projects, programs, and activities for the benefit of the Town and its residents.
The Town Council adopted an Amended and Restated Donation Policy by Resolution No. 26-102, which establishes procedures for the acceptance and administration of donations for public purposes, requires Town Council approval of any donation valued at more than $10,000, and further provides that, regardless of value, if the donor is a contractor or potential contractor, the Town Manager will determine whether the donation should be accepted, rejected, or submitted to the Town Council for approval.
Millworth Group, Inc. (“Millworth”), the contractor for the Bahama Beach Club Condominium Project located at 5371 Estero Boulevard, offered to donate to the Town 180 cubic yards of beach compatible sand originating from that project site.
The sand has already been accepted and is at Bay Oaks. The contractor was required to screen sand to FDEP standard prior to acceptance, and the engineer signed off on it.

description:
On June 15, 2026, the Town Council adopted Resolution No. 26-127, awarding ITB-26-14-PW for Irrigation and Landscaping Installation, Repair, and Maintenance to Tidewater Landscape of Florida, LLC as the lowest, responsive and responsible bidder, and authorizing execution of an Independent Contractor's Agreement. This item was presented to the Town Council as a walk-on item at the regularly scheduled meeting of August 3, 2026, and was approved. The Supplemental Task Authorization was executed by the Town and the Contractor on August 3, 2026. This motion directs the Town Manager to cancel and does not ratify STA No.1 as previously approved.

description:
6200 Estero Blvd Investments, LLC, owner of the subject property, and Fred Drovdlic, AICP, with RVi Planning + Landscape Architecture, applicant, are requesting two applications regarding the change in the 2045 Comprehensive Plan text and Future Land Use Map. The request includes: 1) a small-scale Comprehensive Plan text amendment to the 2045 Comprehensive Plan to create a site-specific Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use District with associated policies; and (2) a small-scale Future Land Use Map amendment from Medium Residential to Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use District.
The property was previously known as the Outrigger Resort. It is zoned CPD and located on the beach side of Estero Blvd. The property was developed with 144 rooms, which was substantially damaged from natural disasters. The CPD was approved by Lee County prior to incorporation of the Town of Fort Myers Beach with density/intensity exceeding the Town’s Comprehensive Plan, as originally adopted following incorporation, and as amended.
The parcel contains land that is seaward of the 1978 Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) and is Recreation FLU and zoned EC. The applicant is not proposing a FLUM amendment for the Recreation FLU portion of the property.
The adopted 2045 Comprehensive Plan included the following policy:
POLICY FLU-1-B2c: “MIXED-USE” - This land use designation is designed for portions of the Town along Estero Boulevard to allow for intense commercial and multifamily residential development. Each mixed-use district is prescribed a maximum density and intensity. To obtain approval for new or expanded commercial activities, proposals must be sensitive to nearby residential uses, contribute to the public realm as described in this comprehensive plan, and meet the design concepts of this plan and the Land Development Code. These qualities and overall consistency with this comprehensive plan shall be evaluated by the Town. Where commercial uses are permitted, residential uses are encouraged on the upper floors. Within the Mixed-Use land use category, all existing “Marina” uses described shall be preserved and allowed to remain on parcels that were zoned for marinas prior to adoption of this plan.
These site-specific Mixed-Use Districts include geographically distinct developments with unique development standards, FARs and densities, including: the Cultural Center, Times Square, Santini Plaza and Center Island Mixed-Use Districts.
In addition to acknowledgment that site-specific districts are an appropriate planning tool to guide future growth and redevelopment, the Comprehensive Plan also includes several policies relating to flexibility for site-specific development proposals, as discussed extensively during the Comprehensive Plan Update process.
The applicant has proposed a new site-specific category under Mixed-Use in the 2045 Comprehensive Plan framework as follows:
f. OUTRIGGER RESORT MIXED-USE (OR-MU) DISTRICT Purpose: The Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use district comprises 3.55+/-acres. The intent of this district is to provide development and redevelopment opportunities for additional residential, resort, commercial, and public and private recreational amenities. Development within this district must be achieved by a unified Commercial Planned Development zoning district and must include contributions to the public realm. The Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use district is envisioned as a residential and resort-oriented lifestyle district with a mix of uses.
The Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use district’s general boundaries are along the Gulf (westside) of Estero Boulevard, approximately two (2) miles north of Big Carlos Pass Bridge and 100-feet south of Fort Myers Beach Access Point 11, and is more specifically described as:
A PARCEL OF LAND LYING IN SECTIONS 33 AND 34, TOWNSHIP 46 SOUTH, RANGE 24 EAST, LEE COUNTY FLORIDA AND BEING MORE PARTICULARLY DESCRIBED AS FOLLOWS:
BEGIN AT THE NORTHEASTERLY CORNER OF LOT 1, FLAMINGO PARK, ACCORDING TO THE PLAT THEREOF, RECORDED IN PLAT BOOK 9, PAGE 66, OF THE PUBLIC RECORDS OF LEE COUNTY, FLORIDA; THENCE RUN N.50°40’49” E., ALONG THE SOUTHEASTERLY LINE OF SAID FLAMINGO PARK, A DISTANCE OF 121.56 FEET TO A POINT ON THE SOUTHWESTERLY RIGHT-OF-WAY LINE OF ESTERO BOULEVARD (COUNTY ROAD 865); THENCE RUN ALONG SAID SOUTHWESTERLY RIGHT-OF-WAY LINE THE FOLLOWING TWO (2) COURSES: 1) SOUTHEASTERLY ALONG A NON-TANGENT CURVE TO THE RIGHT, HAVING A RADIUS OF 2,832.29 FEET, A CENTRAL ANGLE OF 01°40'21", AN ARC LENGTH OF 82.68 FEET, A CHORD LENGTH OF 82.68 FEET, AND A CHORD BEARING OF S. 31°56'13" E. 2) S.31°14'53"E., A DISTANCE OF 270.69 FEET; THENCE DEPARTING SAID SOUTHWESTERLY RIGHT-OF-WAY LINE, RUN S.50°40'49"W., A DISTANCE OF 417.12 FEET TO A POINT ON THE LEE COUNTY COASTAL CONSTRUCTION SETBACK LINE; THENCE RUN ALONG SAID LEE COUNTY COASTAL CONSTRUCTION SETBACK LINE N.39°10'05"W., A DISTANCE OF 350.00 FEET TO THE SOUTHEASTERLY LINE OF SAID FLAMINGO PARK; THENCE DEPARTING SAID LEE COUNTY COASTAL CONSTRUCTION SETBACK LINE, RUN N. 50°40’49” E.,ALONG SAID SOUTHEASTERLY LINE OF SAID FLAMINGO PARK A DISTANCE OF 343.26 FEET TO THE POINT OF BEGINNING.
CONTAINING 154,490.39 SQUARE FEET OR 3.547 ACRES, MORE OR LESS.
Permitted Uses: As limited by the land development regulations, permitted uses include resort and hospitality, lodging/hotel accommodations, residential (multifamily and hotel/condominium), various types of commercial retail to support guests and neighborhood residents such as retail sales and personal service establishments, restaurants (including outdoor dining), live entertainment venues, public access to the beach and passive recreational uses and other contributions to the public realm as identified through Planned Development rezoning. Public benefit uses include: restaurants, bars, retail, event and meeting space, gold cart and bicycle parking, parks, public beach access and coastal storm risk reduction improvement subject to final permitting approval by FEDP.
Height and Stories: The maximum building height is 175 feet measured from Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Lowest Horizontal Structural Member (LHSM) to midpoint of roof and 15 stories inclusive of parking on the first two (2) floors.
Intensity: The floor-to-area ratio (FAR) for the OR-MU district shall not exceed 2.75, subject to the floor-to-area ratio (FAR) calculations in the London Bay Outrigger Commercial Planned Development (CPD) zoning district. Non-residential uses open to the public are limited to 20,000 SF and private non-residential uses are limited to 26,000 SF.
Density: The proposed development is for 150 hotel units and 46 multifamily units. Multi-family units may be converted to hotel units at an equivalency factor of 2.75. The permitted density is 41 dwelling units per acre, subject to the hotel equivalency factor established for the Pedestrian Commercial Future Land Use Category (FLUC) in the Town of Fort Myers Beach Land Development Code (LDC) Section 34-1803(a)(1), and inclusive of hotel, hotel/condominium, and multifamily units (including condominiums, timeshare, vacation clubs and fractional ownership), utilizing the 3.55+/-acres that is part of the Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use district and London Bay Outrigger CPD.
Development Standards: The site design and building development standards for the Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use district will comply with those standards adopted in the Planned Development zoning district.
The companion application will address the FLUM amendment from Medium Residential to Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use District.
On May 12th, 2026, LPA voted (5-2) to recommend denial of case 20240067, a request for a small-scale text amendment to the 2045 Comprehensive Plan to create a site-specific Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use District with associated policies.
The alternative suggestions on the motion were forwarded by the applicant. The new suggestion includes a maximum of 15-story building with FAR 2.5 and a maximum height of 175 feet.
The motion failed 4-3 for Case CPA20240067, a request for a small-scale text amendment to the 2045 Comprehensive Plan to create a site-specific Outrigger Resort Mixed-Use District with associated policies and further changes.
The applicant decided to proceed to the town council with the documents submitted for the April 14th LPA.

description:
6200 Estero Blvd Investments, LLC,(owner) and Fred Drovdlic, AICP, with RVi Planning + Landscape Architecture (applicant) are requesting a rezoning of approximately 3.55 acres, from Commercial Planned Development (CPD) and Commercial Resort (CR) to Outrigger Resort CPD for the development of a mixed use resort. The application includes a new master concept plan for the site.
The subject property was previously developed as the Outrigger Resort. It was zoned CPD and CR and is located on the beach side of Estero Blvd. The parcel contains land that is seaward of the 1978 Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) zoned Environmentally Critical (EC). The applicant is not proposing to rezone the EC portion of the property. The EC portion of the property is addressed by a special exception request for consumption on premises and an Outrigger-Resort bar/chickee hut (open-sided wooden thatched structure).
The existing CPD for the Outrigger Beach Resort was approved through Z-95-085. The previously approved Master Concept Plan (MCP) is not fully legible; therefore, staff relies on applicant-provided documentation; The previous development included 144 hotel efficiency units, and approximately 10,000 square feet of commercial uses. In addition to the hotel use, the allowed uses include bar or cocktail lounge, commercial use of beachfront seaward of the water body setback line, consumption on premises, and convenience store.
The new proposal requests a total of 196 units (150 hotel/condominium and 46 multifamily) and 46,000 square feet of commercial use (private 26,000 SF and public 20,000 SF), and 340 parking spaces. The maximum proposed height is 195 feet as measured by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Lowest Horizontal Structural Member (LHSM) and 15 stories (with parking and mechanical on the first two floors).
The proposed development includes five buildings that range from 15 stories (including 2 stories of parking) to a residential condo and hotel/condominium ranging from 12 stories (with rooftop restaurant), 11, 9 and 3 stories, all including parking. The site plan also includes private club restaurants, a private beach club, an amenity area, and an open deck area.
The application includes a request for 12 deviations from the Land Development Code.
This application is accompanied by other applications including a small-scale Comprehensive Plan text amendment that would create the Outrigger Resort Mixed Use category and a Future Land Use Map amendment from the Medium Residential of the 2045 Comprehensive Plan to the Outrigger Resort Mixed Use category (CPA 20240067); and a Special Exception (SEZ20240112) to allow accessory use and consumption on premises seaward of the Lee County 1978 Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) with the previously mentioned chickee hut beach bar. This structure is proposed to be placed in the same location as a resort structure lost to the hurricanes.
On May 12th, 2026, LPA voted (5-2) to recommend denial of CPD20240061, a request for a rezoning of approximately 3.55 acres, from Commercial Planned Development (CPD) and Commercial Resort (CR) to Outrigger Resort CPD for the development of a Mixed-Use resort due to its inconsistency with the Fort Myers Beach Comprehensive plan. The applicant decided to proceed to the town council with the documents submitted for the April 14th LPA.

Per Town of Fort Myers Beach Code of Ordinances 2-94 as amended by Ordinance 24-17:
Qualifications and Appointment of Members:
In addition to qualifications, which may be specified for membership by state statutes, Charter, ordinance, or resolution, a person appointed to an agency, board, committee, or commission shall give preference to a registered voter within the town's jurisdiction, a property owner within the town's jurisdiction, individuals with specialized experience or knowledge, individuals who have shown interest in the subject matter, or individuals who have a Fort Myers Beach postal code.
(2) Audit committee. All members of the audit committee shall be registered voters within the territorial boundaries of the Town of Fort Myers Beach who do not have any direct financial or business interests involving the town. The town council may waive the residency requirements by majority vote if there are an insufficient number of applicants who reside in the town. All members should, through education and experience, possess a basic understanding of governmental financial reporting and auditing. At least one member of the audit committee shall have accounting, auditing, or related financial management expertise that is specifically relevant to the government sector. The audit committee shall advise the town council on these matters and other matters pursuant to F.S. § 218.391, or any other topics as assigned by the town council.
Committee Purpose
The Audit Committee shall advise the Town Council on matters related to governmental financial reporting and auditing, pursuant to 218.39 F.S., or any other topic(s) as assigned by the Town Council. The Committee helps ensure fiscal accountability and transparency by providing informed recommendations on auditing practices and financial management.
Current Status
There is currently (1) vacancy on the Audit Committee. The Town Clerk's Office has received a total of one application for appointment to the committee.
Public Notice
The community was initially notified of the vacancies at the Town Council Management and Planning Meeting on August 4, 2025, and subsequently on the Town's website and through social media posts, with applications due to the Town Clerk's Office by the close of business on Wednesday, July 15, 2026.

description:
Fernando Virto, the owner of the property located at 100/102 Bay Mar Drive, is requesting a variance from Table 34-3 of the Land Development Code (LDC) to reduce the required 20-foot rear setback by 7.9 feet to allow a rear setback of 12.1 feet for an enclosed access staircase extending to the second floor of a proposed two-family residence within the Residential Conservation (RC) zoning district.
The property is a corner lot situated at the intersection of Estero Boulevard and Bay Mar Drive. The lot is an irregularly shaped corner lot, with a depth ranging from 101 to 75 feet, and a width ranging from 97 feet to 100 feet. The property is currently vacant, and prior to Hurricane Ian, the property contained a duplex constructed in the early 1980s. The subject property is a conforming lot in RC zoning district. Based on available Lee County Property Appraiser aerial imagery, the previously existing duplex appears to have contained nonconforming rear setbacks.
The applicant is proposing the construction of a new two-family residence that includes an enclosed staircase extending to the second floor in the rear setback. As proposed, the enclosed staircase would maintain a rear setback of 12.1 feet where 20 feet is required. The applicant is, therefore, requesting a variance of 7.9 feet from the required rear setback to allow the proposed enclosed staircase encroachment.
During the LPA hearing on June 16, the LPA voted 6-1 to recommend approval with conditions of the variance request from LDC Table 34-3, to reduce the required 20-foot rear setback by 7.9 feet and allow a rear setback of 12.1 feet for an enclosed access staircase extending to the second floor of a proposed two-family residence within the Residential Conservation (RC) zoning district.

description:
The Neighborhood Company, on behalf of FMBH, LLC, is requesting approval of a Development Agreement with deviations for redevelopment of the former Wyndham/Holiday Inn property located at 6890 Estero Boulevard. The proposal includes a phased redevelopment consisting of a restaurant, open-air entertainment venue, recreation uses, accessory parking, and future joint parking operations.
Phase 1: Open a restaurant and entertainment venue with recreational uses as quickly as possible. In order to expedite the opening of this venue, temporary mobile vending trailers will be utilized to comply with FEMA and Florida Building code flood regulations.
Phase 2: This phase will require the design, permitting and construction of a wave dissipation wall combined with a flood map revision to change the property’s flood zone from VE to AE. The map change will allow for construction of permanent dry flood-proofed structures that will replace and eliminate the use of temporary trailers. Additionally, the recreation uses will be expanded to include a pool and lazy river. The two phases are described in more detail below.
The underlying zoning for this property is Commercial Resort, which has housed hotels like Holiday Inn and Wyndham Garden since 1969. The property was severely damaged during the hurricane Ian in 2022. The owner of the property believes that the highest and best use for this property was and remains a resort hotel. However, the current conditions remain unfavorable financially to establish a resort hotel. As a result, the Development Agreement will allow limited uses outlined in Phase 1 and 2, (depicted in Exhibits C and D) of the agreement. However, the agreement also includes permitted uses under the current CR zoning district, including Commercial Resort, but those uses cannot be developed/constructed unless the Development Agreement is amended or terminated.
On June 16, 2026, LPA voted 6-1 to recommend approval with conditions for Development Agreement request with 7 deviations, DA20250277, to allow the redevelopment of a restaurant and a family entertainment venue on the Old Wyndham/Holiday Inn property. The request is Phased Development.
The Local Planning Agency (LPA) recommended that the following conditions be incorporated into the Development Agreement:
Include a defined timeline for completion of Phase 1 in the Development Agreement.
Require both the ingress and egress access points to include paved driveway aprons.
Require a parking attendant to be present onsite during all operating hours.
Require public restrooms remain locked when the facility is closed and outside operating hours.
Require the applicant to evaluate alternative landscaping enhancements, including larger landscape planters, where feasible and subject to approval by the Town Engineer.
Require submission of an updated traffic impact analysis as part of the Phase 2 Development Order application.
Add the Lee County Department of Transportation to the list of required governmental agencies from which permits or approvals must be obtained prior to development.
Applicants provided a revised version of the DA and site plan on the 9th of July.

description:
The Neighborhood Company, on behalf of TPI-FMB Suites LLC, is requesting rezoning of the property located at 1207 Estero Boulevard from the Downtown zoning district to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) for redevelopment of the historic Silver Sands Resort. The property consists of approximately 0.74 acres and is identified as STRAP #19-46-24-W4-0150D.0050. The Future Land Use designation is Times Square Mixed-use Commercial, and the property is located within the Downtown zoning district.
The historic Silver Sands Resort previously consisted of approximately 22 lodging units, including cottages and villas, along with accessory commercial uses and docks. The site was substantially damaged during Hurricane Ian in 2022.
The proposed application includes a new Master Concept Plan (MCP) for the site consisting of:
A 60-unit boutique hotel (This is approximately a 173% increase in density (from 22 units to 60 units))
Approximately 2,500 square feet of ground-floor commercial space,
46 onsite parking spaces,
Rooftop pool and amenity deck,
Canal-side activation area and dock improvements,
Streetscape and pedestrian improvements along Estero Boulevard and Primo Drive.
According to Comprehensive plan 2045, the allowed density for Time Square mixed-use development is 6 units per acre. However, the MCP is proposing approximately 81 units per acre; that is almost 12 times higher density than permitted by the code.
The proposed maximum building height will be approximately 58 feet as measured from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Lowest Horizontal Structural Member (LHSM), with an overall building height of approximately 70 feet from grade to the roof peak. The building will consist of six stories, including a ground-level parking floor. The maximum height will be limited to the center of the building and the majority of the structure, front and rear, will be stepped down and limited to 5 stories.
On June 16, 2026, LPA voted unanimously (7-0) to recommend approval with conditions for CPD amendment request with 11 deviations, CPA 20250286, to rezone the property from Downtown to commercial planned development for the redevelopment of Silver Sands Resort.

attachments.name: 26-167, Establishment of Charter School Application Ad Hoc Committees
Overview of Charter School Application Committees
Charter School Ad Hoc Committees Application

description:
In response to ongoing Interlocal Agreement (ILA) negotiations with the Lee County School Board regarding the conveyance of school property, the Town of Fort Myers Beach has pursued a parallel track to explore a charter school model for the community. During prior proceedings, the Superintendent of Schools expressed openness to exploring a charter school as a potential pathway for restoring educational services on Fort Myers Beach, which provided the impetus for the Town to formalize an application development process.
Consistent with this direction, the Town Council accepted a donation of charter consultant services from the Education Freedom Foundation during the Town Manager's comments at a prior meeting. Because these consultant services were donated at no cost to the Town, this item carries no financial impact to the municipality.
The resolution before the Town Council establishes six Ad Hoc Committees to provide structured, subject-matter assistance in preparing a charter school application in compliance with Florida Statutes Section 1002.33 and Florida Administrative Code Rule 6A-6.0786. The application must conform to Rule 6A-6.0786, F.A.C., which became effective in August 2024, and must utilize Form IEPC-M1 as prescribed by the Florida Department of Education. The six Ad Hoc committees established under this resolution are as follows:
Governance Committee — Responsible for Application Section 10, the Statement of Assurances, Board Member Information Forms, Addendums, and the Chart of Attachments (Pages 21–23 and 35–45 of the application). Staff liaison support is provided by Executive Leadership and Legal.
Educational Program Committee — Responsible for Application Sections 1 through 9 (Pages 9–20), addressing the school's educational mission, curriculum, assessment, and instructional design in alignment with Section 1002.33, Florida Statutes. Staff liaison support is provided by Executive Leadership.
Operations & Human Capital Committee — Responsible for Application Sections 11, 12, and 13 (Pages 23–25), covering staffing plans, employee qualifications, and performance evaluation systems consistent with Section 1012.34, Florida Statutes (Student Success Act). Staff liaison support is provided by Human Resources.
Community Engagement Committee — Responsible for Application Sections 14 and 15 (Pages 26–28), addressing community outreach, parent and stakeholder involvement, and dispute resolution procedures pursuant to Sections 1001.42(8)(c), 1002.20, and 1014.04, Florida Statutes. Staff liaison support is provided by Communications and Community Engagement.
Facilities, Safety & Operations Committee — Responsible for Application Sections 16, 17, 18, and 19 (Pages 29–30), addressing facility requirements, safe-school officer obligations under Section 1006.12, Florida Statutes (Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School Public Safety Act), active assailant response planning under Section 1006.07(6), Florida Statutes, and threat management team requirements under Section 1006.07(7), Florida Statutes. Staff liaison support is provided by Community Development and Emergency Management.
Finance & Business Operations Committee — Responsible for Application Sections 20, 21, and 22 (Pages 31–34), covering the school's budget, financial management, and audit compliance in accordance with Section 218.39, Florida Statutes. Staff liaison support is provided by the Finance Team.
Each Ad Hoc committee must be composed of a minimum of three members, drawn from residents and/or subject-matter experts, and each committee shall include one Town staff liaison and one member of the Town Clerk's Office. All committee members must satisfy five general eligibility requirements as outlined in the supporting documentation. All committee proceedings are subject to Chapter 119, Florida Statutes (Public Records Law) and Section 286.011, Florida Statutes (Government in the Sunshine Law).
The application development process follows a structured timeline and workflow:
August 3, 2026 — Town Council approves the charter advisory committees; volunteer applications open immediately.
September 10, 2026 — Applications due to the Town Clerk at Town of Fort Myers Beach, Attn: Town Clerk, 6231 Estero Boulevard, Fort Myers Beach, FL 33931.
September 23, 2026 — Town Council reviews and appoints committee members.
October 6, 2026, at 1:30 PM — Town Staff hosts Sunshine Law training for all appointed committee members.
Mid-October 2026 — Committees begin meeting on a bi-monthly (twice per month) basis.
Upon completion of committee work, the application follows a five-stage workflow process: (1) the Town of Fort Myers Beach coordinates, integrates, and compiles committee work into a comprehensive charter application; (2) the Education Freedom Foundation reviews, refines, and provides expert guidance on the compiled application; (3) the Town incorporates consultant feedback and finalizes the application; (4) the Town Council reviews and votes to approve the application for submission; and (5) the finalized application is submitted to the School District of Lee County for review. Should the School District request revisions, the application routes back through the Town Council for further action. Upon completion, the application is submitted to Dr. Denise Carlin, Superintendent of Schools, at the Lee County Public Education Center, 2855 Colonial Boulevard, Fort Myers, FL 33966-1012.
The committees shall remain active until one of two termination conditions is met: (1) the charter school application is approved by the School District of Lee County, or (2) the Town Council moves to decommission the committees.

attachments.name: 20250902 Fort Myers Beach Task 6 Adaptation Plan

description:
Charlotte County, on behalf of CHNEP, desires to engage the Town of Fort Myers Beach to provide services on a project-specific basis to support CHNEP’s Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan and annual Work Plans, as they may be amended from time to time. This Interlocal Agreement will serve as a Master Agreement between Charlotte County and the Town of Fort Myers Beach, with specific support services to be designated, scoped, and compensated under individual Work Assignments issued and mutually agreed upon by the parties.
Pursuant to a Work Assignment issued under this Interlocal Agreement, the Town is seeking professional engineering services to evaluate the performance of the existing stormwater management systems within Focus Area 15 (Indian Bayou) and Focus Area 16 (Ibis Street), as identified in the Town’s 2025 Vulnerability Assessment and Adaptation Plan, and to develop engineering solutions that reduce flooding, improve water quality, minimize pollutant transport into coastal waters, and enhance resilience, at an estimated project cost of $200,000.00.
The services to be performed under this Work Assignment support Actions WQI-3, FW-2, and E-4 of CHNEP’s Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan, in coordination with Lee County partners. The services performed under this Work Assignment will be funded through CHNEP grant funds administered by Charlotte County, and, pursuant to Section III(C) of this Agreement, Charlotte County shall pay all invoices on behalf of CHNEP from CHNEP funds, such that the Town of Fort Myers Beach will incur no cost to the Town under this Agreement or the associated Work Assignment.
The Town's Draft Focus Areas exhibit and associated sensitivity ranking, prepared as part of the Vulnerability Assessment, delineate Focus Area 15 (Indian Bayou) and Focus Area 16 (Ibis Street) as containing critical Town assets, including wastewater lift stations, water utility conveyance systems, and wetlands, and reflect Town staff feedback identifying these areas for further stormwater evaluation.
The Adaptation Plan's Focus Area Rankings ranked Focus Area 16 (Ibis Street) 5th of 18 Town-wide focus areas, with a total evaluation score of 16, and Focus Area 15 (Indian Bayou) 8th of 18, with a total evaluation score of 5, reflecting critical asset vulnerability to flooding, current and future zoning, and the extent of existing, ongoing, and planned stormwater projects in each area.
The Adaptation Plan identifies updating the Town's Stormwater Master Plan, in conjunction with an updated Town-wide stormwater network model, as among the Town's top priority adaptation needs, in order to define where stormwater improvements are most needed and to direct the Town's Capital Improvement Plan and budget allocations.

The additional Service Location Licenses are needed to accommodate the Town's growing number of billable utility service locations, ensuring the platform continues to support the full scope of accounts under management without disruption to billing operations.
