description:
Himmelstein Associates, LLC, Robert Himmelstein, and Stephanie Himmelstein (the "Himmelsteins") have filed a Second Renewed Administrative Appeal of a building permit(s) #242333/#234477 issued for construction of an enclosed elevated pool at property located at 21391 Widgeon Terrace, Fort Myers Beach, Florida. The property is owned by the Himmelsteins' neighbor Todd R. Plaisted as Trustee for the Todd R. Plaisted Trust (“Plaisted”). The appeal has been pending since December 2024. Resolution of the appeal was delayed by the Town Council pending the judicial review of variances granted by the Town Council to authorize the construction of the pool. On appeal, the circuit court upheld the Town Council's approval of the variance. The Himmelsteins appealed the circuit court decision, which was denied by the 6th Judicial Court of Appeal. In addition, the Himmelsteins provided notice to the Town that the surveyor, who prepared the survey at issue was disciplined by the Florida Department of Agriculture & Consumer Services, Board of PRofessional Surveyors and Mappers for errors in the survey. The survey was corrected and Town staff determined that the errors did not impact the validity of the granted variances and took no further action in response to the Himmelstein's notice.
During preparation of the appeal, Town staff and the parties noted there was a procedural issue related to the Town Council's jurisdiction to address the appeal of the building permit under Ordinance 24-30 that was amended in 2024 to authorize the Town's Code Enforcement Special Magistrate's to adjudicate appeals of building official decisions. Plaisted's attorney has filed a Motion to Dismiss the pending appeal on the grounds that the Town Council lacks jurisdiction. The Himmelsteins, through their attorney, have filed a response in opposition. This appeal is the first application of the recently adopted change to the review process of building official decisions, which merits direction from the Town Council as to its application of building official appeals. The change to the review process of building official decisions was due to the fact that the Interlocal Agreement with the Lee County Board of Adjustment and Appeals had expired and an impartial fact-finder was needed to fulfill this role. The Town Attorney has previously provided her opinion regarding application of Ordinance 24-30 to the current facts; however, the Himmelstein's attorney has raised some issued that merit comment by the Town Council as well as resolution of the pending Motion to Dismiss prior to a review of the merits of the appeal.
For purposes of efficiency, the parties and the Town Attorney have agreed that the review of the Motion to Dismiss should be reviewed by the Town Council at a separate hearing from the merits on the appeal. If the Town Council grants the Motion to Dismiss, the appeal is concluded. If the Town Council denies the appeal, the Town Council should identify a date for a hearing on the Second Renewed Administrative Appeal of a building permit(s) #242333/#234477 or transfer the case to the Special Magistrate for further disposition.

description:
Over the past year, staff have received several inquiries from local contractors and builders regarding Florida Power & Light (FP&L) requirements for installing electric meters above FEMA-required flood elevations and providing access to these elevated meters. These updated FP&L requirements have resulted in encroachments into required setbacks on residential lots.
Based on these concerns, staff initiated drafting of an ordinance to amend the Land Development Code (LDC). The proposed amendment incorporates electric meter equipment and associated access structures into Article III, Division 3, Section 34-638(d)(1)(g), which addresses exceptions to setback and dimensional standards for mechanical equipment. Additionally, the amendment establishes five criteria to govern situations where meter installations, including associated platforms and access stairways, encroach on required side and rear setbacks.
This text amendment will provide an alternative and quicker solution to the full variance process for these resiliency-related efforts.
At May 12, 2026, LPA meeting, the ordinance 26-09 with proposed changes was unanimously approved.
At the June 1st, 2026, Town Council meeting the ordinance 26-09 was heard and requests from councilors to correct scrivener’s errors and provide additional language to disallow any entrance into the home from the FP&L access stairs and landing. The vote was 5-0 to move the ordinance to the next Council meeting.

description:
Following Hurricane Ian (FEMA Disaster Declaration 4673-DR-FL), the Town of Fort Myers Beach applied for Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) funding to elevate twenty-five (25) single-family residences located within Special Flood Hazard Areas (SFHA) on Estero Island. FEMA awarded this project on March 11, 2026. The Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM) serves as the pass-through entity and has transmitted Sub-Recipient Agreement H1360 for execution.
The total project cost is $7,933,678.00, structured as a 75/25 federal-to-local cost share. The federal obligation under this agreement is $5,688,229.25 (75%), with a non-federal match requirement of $1,983,419.50 (25%). An additional $21,316.25 in Sub-Recipient Management Costs (SRMC) is included at 100% federal funding. The Period of Performance runs from November 2, 2023, through May 31, 2028.
The scope of work requires elevating each of the 25 participating residential structures to a minimum of two feet above Base Flood Elevation (BFE), including foundation work, utility disconnection and reconnection, permitting, and all required inspections and closeout documentation. Six properties require coastal VE Zone foundation design to account for wave action and scour; four properties require lift platform installation due to medical conditions of the homeowners.

description: The original Resolution 25-235 did not address the large meters because they were up to date with the radio frequency technology. Approval of resolution 25-299, converting from radio frequency style meters to a cellular-based meter, was only for 5/8 and 1 inch meters (original contract). It is necessary to install and convert the remaining meters in the system to the new technology. The meters that remain are the larger meters in the system, 1 1/2, 2, 3, 4, 6 inch meters. description:
John W. Richard, on behalf of Richard John W. TR, the owner of 1161/1165 Estero Blvd, is requesting a variance from LDC Section 34-676(a), to multiply the parking requirements by 0% and allow a 100% reduction in parking requirements where a maximum percentage of 67% is multiplied with parking requirements to allow a 33% parking reduction by right for properties in the Downtown zoning district.
The subject property is an irregularly shaped parcel located at the northeast corner of Estero Boulevard and Crescent Street, both of which are identified as primary streets within the Town’s Land Development Code. The property currently supports a mixed-use development with approximately 2,700 square feet of ground-floor retail and three residential rental units on the second level. The site currently provides four on-site parking spaces, including one ADA parking space, and maintains a joint parking agreement for three additional spaces with a nearby property located at 150 Crescent Street.
The applicant is seeking relief due to existing site constraints and operational safety concerns. The current parking configuration requires vehicles to back out of the site directly into the intersection of Estero Boulevard and Crescent Street. Due to limited site depth, approximately 6.5 feet of the backing maneuver occurs within the Town’s right-of-way, creating a conflict between vehicular movements and intersection traffic. Therefore, the applicant is requesting a variance from LDC Section 34-676(a), to multiply the parking requirements by 0% to allow a 100% reduction in parking requirements. Approval of this request will allow the Applicant to remove the existing parking and replace it with pedestrian-oriented improvements including outdoor patio or seating areas.
During the LPA hearing on April 21, the LPA voted 5-0 to recommend denial of the variance request from LDC Section 34-676(a), to multiply the parking requirements by 0% and allow a 100% reduction in parking requirements where a maximum percentage of 67% is multiplied with parking requirements to allow a 33% parking reduction by right for properties in the Downtown zoning district. The LPA unanimously recommended denial, finding that the request does not meet the requirements of LDC Section 34-87, and that the requested variance is not the minimum variance that will relieve the applicant of an unreasonable burden caused by the application of the regulation in question to his property.

description:
Over the past year, staff have received several inquiries from local contractors and builders regarding Florida Power & Light (FP&L) requirements for installing electric meters above FEMA-required flood elevations and providing access to these elevated meters. These updated FP&L requirements have resulted in encroachments into required setbacks on residential lots.
Based on these concerns, staff initiated drafting of an ordinance to amend the Land Development Code (LDC). The proposed amendment incorporates electric meter equipment and associated access structures into Article III, Division 3, Section 34-638(d)(1)(g), which addresses exceptions to setback and dimensional standards for mechanical equipment. Additionally, the amendment establishes five criteria to govern situations where meter installations, including associated platforms and access stairways, encroach on required side and rear setbacks.
This text amendment will provide an alternative and quicker solution to the full variance process for these resiliency-related efforts.
At May 12, 2026, LPA meeting, the ordinance 26-09 with proposed changes was unanimously approved.

description:
Section 13.03 of Article 13 of the Town of Fort Myers Beach Charter provides that the Town’s charter shall be reviewed at least every 10 years by a 5-member charter review commission to be appointed and funded by the Town Council. During its public meeting on June 2, 2025, the Town Council appointed 5 members and 2 alternates to serve as the Fort Myers Beach Charter Review Commission (“Charter Commission”). The Charter Commission held its first meeting on October 7, 2025 and reviewed the entirety of the Town of Ft Myers Beach Charter over the following months until its last meeting on April 7, 2026. The Chair of the Charter Commission presented the Commission’s recommendations for changes to 5 Sections of the Town Charter to the Town Council on April 20, 2026. The Town Council directed the Town Attorney to draft proposed charter amendments consistent with the recommendation of the Charter Commission and Florida law, or in the alternative present the Town Council with proposed ordinances or resolutions to implement the policies underlying the recommendation changes proposed by the Charter Commission.
Charter Change 1: This Charter change is recommended to emphasize the need for transparency and ethical behavior when elected and appointed members of the Town’s committees, agencies, commissions, etc. The CRC recognizes that the town already has adopted ordinances to implement its concerns; however, it believes that the policies and values embedded in those ordinances should also be included in the Charter.
Charter Change 2: This Charter change is recommended to vest in an independent committee of Town residents the ability to recommend increases in base salary for elected Town Council members.
Charter Change 3: This Charter change is recommended to clarify the term of an individual appointed to fill a vacant Town Council seat. Currently, the Charter provides for an interim appointment until the next general election.
Charter Change 4: The Charter change would extend the term of the appointment through the unexpired term of the vacated Town Council seat.
Charter Change 5: This Charter change is to eliminate outdated provisions.
Charter Change 6: This Charter change is to eliminate outdated language.
This ordinance is on a tight adoption timeline due to the need to provide a timely delivery to the Lee County Supervisor of Elections for inclusion on the November 2026 ballot.
At the May 18, 2026 first reading public hearing, the Town Council voted to approve the draft ordinance for second reading on June 1, 2026 with one change to Question 2 on page 6: the number of years from 3 to 4.
The Town Attorney has confirmed that only the title and ballot summary will appear on the ballot and not the proposed charter language included in the proposed ordinance.

description:
Originally, September 9 and September 23, 2026 were proposed as hearing dates. September 9 was determined to be unavailable due to a scheduling conflict among Council members. While September 23 had been considered as a potential second hearing date, it cannot be confirmed as a viable option until a first hearing date is established.
The statutory advertising restrictions governing the second hearing are directly dependent upon when the first hearing is held. Specifically, the second hearing must be advertised within 15 days of the first hearing and held no fewer than 2 days and no more than 5 days after that advertisement is published. Staff therefore recommends holding the First (Tentative) Budget Hearing on Monday, September 14, 2026 and the Second (Final) Budget Hearing on Monday, September 28, 2026, both at 5:01 p.m. The 14-day interval between the two proposed hearing dates accommodates the required advertisement period and ensures full compliance with Section 200.065(2)(e)2., F.S. Any compliant alternative timeline that satisfies all statutory requirements may also be considered by the Council.
___________
The Town is required by Florida Statute and the Town Charter to conduct two public hearings annually for the purpose of adopting an operating budget, capital budget, and ad valorem millage rate. This process is governed by Section 200.065, Florida Statutes (the Truth in Millage, or "TRIM," law), Rule 12D-17 of the Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.), and Sections 11.02 and 11.03 of the Town Charter. The Town Charter, Article XI, establishes the financial procedures framework within which the budget process must operate, including the requirement that the Town Manager submit a proposed budget to the Council on or before July 15 of each year. The TRIM process requires coordination among multiple taxing authorities within Lee County to avoid scheduling conflicts. Under state law, the Lee County School Board holds first priority for budget hearing dates, the Lee County Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) holds second priority, and all other taxing authorities — including the Town of Fort Myers Beach — may not schedule their public hearings on dates already claimed by either the School Board or the BOCC, pursuant to Section 200.065(2)(e)2., F.S.
Florida law establishes strict parameters governing when and how budget hearings may be held:
All budget public hearings must be held after 5:00 p.m. on weekdays (Monday through Friday), or at any time on Saturday, pursuant to Section 200.065(2)(e)2., F.S. Hearings may not be held on Sundays.
The Lee County School Board has first priority in selecting budget hearing dates.
The Lee County Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) has second priority and may not schedule hearings on dates the School Board has reserved.
No other taxing authority in Lee County — including the Town of Fort Myers Beach — may use hearing dates already claimed by the School Board or the BOCC, pursuant to Section 200.065(2)(e)2., F.S.65

Florida Forest Service Technical Assistance Proposal

description:
The Florida Forest Service has offered the Town the services of Natural Resource Planning Services Inc, dba Legacy Arborist Services (LAS), to prepare a tree canopy analysis, tree inventory and management plan ("Tree Analysis") for Town of Fort Myers Beach in accordance with the Proposal from LAS, a copy of which is attached as Exhibit A to the Resolution. In exchange for the Tree Analysis, the Florida Forest Service requires the Town to engage in urban forestry best practices, including, but not limited to, planting trees and maintenance activities in the same amount as the Florida Forest Service will pay LAS for the Tree Analysis. The Florida Forest Service has advised the Town that documentation of the Town's expenditure for the implementation of urban forestry best practices will satisfy the Town's in kind match for the Tree Analysis in the same amount as charged by LAS.
The Town is already under contract with Earth Balance Corporation to provide dune plantings in the amount not to exceed $605,579.50. The Town's payment to Earth Balance Corporation for future plantings in the same amount of LAS's services will suffice as the required exchange for the Tree Analysis.
The Tree Canopy Analysis will be completed for area defined within the jurisdictional limits of the Town of Fort Myers Beach. The methodology will involve using random point sampling from aerial images. The data collected will provide insight into the percentage of canopy coverage and include valuable details on the environmental benefits of the canopy. Deliverables will include a tree inventory in ESRI GIS shapefile format. The Tree Canopy Analysis will address 1) tree canopy; 2) a tree inventory; and 3) a Urban Forestry Management Plan.
The Urban Forestry Management Plan ("UFMP") will provide a comprehensive guidance document to support the Town’s efforts to sustain the health, appearance, and function of the Town’s urban forest. The outcome of the UFMP is for the Town of Fort Myers Beach urban forest to be preserved, enhanced, and properly managed, providing the greatest possible benefit to the residents of the Town of Fort Myers Beach. The UFMP is also intended to align with the American Public Works Association’s (APWA) Urban Forestry Best Management Practices for Public Works Managers while adapting to the unique needs of the Town of Fort Myers Beach. The UFMP shall define and outline operational activities for managing tree assets and support decision-making, funding strategies, and performance tracking. TheUFMP shall connect urban forest management to the Town's overall goals, outline tracking and maintenance practices, and support resource allocation decisions to meet both community and internal stakeholder needs.

description:
The Town of Fort Myers Beach (TOWN) provides stormwater management throughout the TOWN’s jurisdiction and has been working over the past several years to make improvements. One area of concern has been Carlos Circle, which is located towards the north end of the island.The Carlos Circle Drainage Improvements project was previously initiated under Supplemental Task Authorization No. 4. Since that time, portions of the project have been completed, including partial construction of the outfall system and preparation of design documents. Due to the continuation of the project into a new fiscal year, this scope provides for completion of design finalization, permitting, and construction phase support.
The project consists of drainage improvements to alleviate flooding within the Carlos Circle neighborhood through a combination of stormwater conveyance, outfall improvements, and water quality treatment enhancements.
Since the original authorization, regulatory criteria have been updated, and the project will be required to comply with the current South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD) Environmental Resource Permit (ERP) rules. As a result, additional stormwater treatment considerations will be necessary. The CONSULTANT shall evaluate the need for, and incorporate as required, additional Best Management Practices (BMPs) and stormwater treatment components to meet current water quality and treatment standards.
This scope of services includes design, permitting and construction oversight for the proposed improvements. It is understood that the proposed improvements will be performed as a change order with the Contractor currently performing improvements on “Tier 1”.

description:
What’s Up FMB is requesting approval for the Coastal Cars & Coffee Summer Series, a recurring community event featuring classic and specialty vehicles at Santini Marina Plaza located at 7205 Estero Boulevard on May 23, June 20, July 18, August 15, and September 19, 2026, from 8:30 AM to 11:00 AM.
The event is designed as a low-impact, family-friendly gathering that allows residents and visitors to enjoy a curated vehicle showcase while supporting local businesses and encouraging visitation to the south end of Fort Myers Beach. Attendance is expected to include approximately 30–50 registered vehicles with an estimated 200 spectators. There is a planned food truck to accompany the event.
Participants will stage and display vehicles at Santini Marina Plaza before departing in a coordinated cruise along Estero Boulevard under normal traffic conditions and in partnership with the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, with no road closures requested. Overflow parking is proposed through the rental of 22 parking spaces at Beach Access 36 (Wastina Way), from 8:30 AM to 2:00 PM, while primary parking will be accommodated onsite and at partner locations (such as the Whale).
Event staff will manage parking flow, participant coordination, and cleanup, with no alcohol service, or major amplified entertainment associated with the event. The event is intended to provide a positive economic impact for nearby businesses while maintaining minimal disruption to surrounding properties and public access.

description:
Hold all hearings after 5:00 p.m., Monday – Friday, or anytime on Saturday. Do not hold hearings on Sunday (s. 200.065(2)(e)2., F.S.).
The BOCC cannot schedule its hearings on days the school board has hearings scheduled. The school board has first priority of a hearing date and the BOCC has second (s. 200.065(2)(e)2., F.S.).
No other taxing authority in the county can use for its public hearings the hearing dates the BCC and the school board have scheduled (s. 200.065(2)(e)2., F.S.).
Lee County School Board budget hearing dates are Tuesday, July 29, 2025, and Tuesday, September 9, 2025.
Lee County Board of County Commissioners budget hearing dates are Thursday, September 4, 2025, and Tuesday, September 16, 2025.
According to the Florida Department of Revenue Trim Compliance Workbook which presents the Trim Requirements found in Chapter 200, F.S., and Rule 12D-17, Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.), and in accordance with Sections 11.02 and 11.03 of the Town Charter regarding the budget, the following time-line must be adhered to:
July 1st: Property Appraiser Delivers Certification of Taxable Value (Form DR-420) to the Town
July 15th: Town Manager Delivers Proposed Budget to Town Council
August 4th: Town must certify Maximum Millage Rate
September 3rd -18th: First (Tentative) Budget Hearing regarding Tentative Budget and Proposed Millage Rate must be held
September 4th - 26th: Advertise Second Budget Hearing to Adopt Final Budget and Final Millage Rate within 15 days after First (Tentative) Budget Hearing
September 6th–30th : Hold Second Budget Hearing within 2–5 days after the advertisement for the Second Budget Hearing
September 30th: Deadline for Adopting Final Budget and Millage Rate
Suggest holding Budget Hearings at 5:01 pm on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, and Wednesday, September 23, 2026, but any similar timeline that fits within the guidelines above may be chosen.
Given that the Town is only provided with an estimated taxable value at the beginning of June, it may be best to wait to determine the Maximum Millage Rate until after the Town receives the Certified Taxable Value from the Tax Appraiser on July 1st. Since the Maximum Millage Rate needs to be set on or before August 4th, the Town Council could choose to meet in July to vote on the Maximum Millage Rate, or it could choose to wait until the deadline of August 4th, which would be one day after its first meeting in August.

attachments.name: NS Final 26-102, Resolution Amending and Restating Town's Donation Policy

description: The Town Council and its Advisory Committees are periodically asked to accept monetary or in-kind donations for Town projects and events. At the February 5, 2026, Management and Planning public meeting, the Town Council reviewed the Town's existing donation policy approved in 2011. Two features highlighted during the discussion of the existing policy were the amount of a donation which could be accepted by the Town Manager ($10,000) without Town Council involvement and a gift giving catalog, which contained a wish list of things needed by various department in the Town. During the discussion, the need for public recognition of the donation, documentation and consideration of any financial burden (one-time or ongoing) on the Town and whether the Town should accept donations with restrictions. Direction was given to the Town Attorney to draft an amendment to affirmatively state that any solicitation of funds or goods would not in any manner influence any decision to be made by the Town staff, Manager or Council. The Town Manager indicated he would bring any significant donations to the Town Council's attention during a public meeting even if below the $10,000 limit. Lastly, any donation that was also seeking name recognition could only be approved by the Town Council.

description:
From the Request for Qualifications: The Town of Fort Myers Beach (the "Town") seeks qualifications from professional Landscape Architecture and design firms to provide comprehensive design, permitting, and construction-phase engineering and inspection (CEI) services for the Parks and Recreation Revitalization Project. This project, funded in part through Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) funds, aims to restore, improve, and modernize public recreation facilities that were severely impacted by Hurricane Ian. The firm selected will provide professional services for the Redevelopment of the Newton Park Beach Facility.
The successful firm must have experience in post-disaster infrastructure restoration, flood mitigation planning, resilient and sustainable design, and compliance with federal procurement and CDBG-DR regulations.
Through this solicitation, the Town seeks an experienced, engineering, and design firm to provide comprehensive professional services that align with FEMA flood mitigation guidelines, CDBG-DR program requirements, and sustainable development best practices. The project will not only restore these vital community assets but also integrate resilient infrastructure solutions to protect against future climate-related threats.
Pursuant to Sec. 2-480(h)(1) of the Town's Code of Ordinances and the Consultant's Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA), contracts for professional services consisting of Architecture, Professional Engineering, Landscape Architecture or Registered Land Surveying must be competitively negotiated in accordance with the requirements of Section 287.055 F.S. within statutory thresholds. In addition, the Town competitively bids for other professional services as further described below.
The Town re-solicited this project under RFQ-25-17-AD, with responses due in October 2025 and the Town receiving four responses from Chen Moore and Associates, EnSite, Inc., Kimley-Horn and Associates Inc., and JR Evans Engineering P.A..
In accordance with the Town of Fort Myers Beach Purchasing Ordinance 26-06, Sec 2-480 (14) the Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) consisting of a minimum of three members, may be established for the purpose of evaluating bids submitted to the Town. All members of the SAC are prohibited from speaking, answering questions or having contact with any potential bidder. The SAC will review the bid and response materials prior to the SAC meeting. The committee evaluates each firm's qualifications based on past experience, express understanding of the project and proposed method of handling the project and any other criteria included for evaluation.
The Town's SAC, consisting of the Deputy Town Manager, Community Services Director, and Community Development Director, was established for the purpose of evaluating the Request for Qualifications proposals received by the Town, and met on the 13th day of November 2025 to evaluate each firm's qualifications. At the noticed public meeting, the firms were publicly evaluated based upon the established criteria within the Request for Qualifications document, and the SAC short-listed three firms were then invited for a public interview and discussion, which occurred on February 11, 2026, in which the Selection Advisory Committee announced and deemed an ordered list of JR Evans Engineering P.A., Kimley-Horn and Associates, and Chen Moore and Associates to be the most responsive and qualified to perform the required services after their evaluation as a recommendation to the Town Manager. The SAC also held a meeting on December 18th to clarify the interview process in preparation of their interview meeting.
The Town Manager, after reviewing the SAC recommendation, forwarded this to the Town Council for consideration during a regularly scheduled meeting. The Town Council reviewed the rankings and qualifications of the firms and voted to accept the rankings by the Town Manager. The Town Council also direct the Town Manager or designee to initiate negotiations with the top ranked firm JR Evans Engineering, P.A. and after negotiations and Lee County approval of the draft agreement, the agreement is now going before the Town Council for final approval.

description:
The Town Manager on behalf of the Town entered into an agreement with Goldman Wolfe, LLC on June 2, 2025, to provide financial consulting services following the departure of the Town’s key finance personnel to ensure the continuity of critical financial operations, including audit support, budget preparation, grant management, month-end close processes, and the timely processing of vendor payments.
The original Agreement provided for payment of services not to exceed $50,000, which was within the Town Manager’s authority.
A first amendment to the agreement was approved by Town Council on August 4, 2025, to increase the not-to-exceed amount from $50,000 to $197,600 and to include a penalty of $5,000 for breach of the Agreement during an emergency recovery period as required by Section 252.505, Florida Statutes.
Ongoing vacancies of critical finance positions have necessitated the continued use of Goldman & Wolfe, LLC. resources beyond the not-to-exceed amount since September 15, 2025, totaling approximately $213,700 for services rendered from September 15, 2025 through May 18, 2026, and which have been funded by payroll savings achieved through vacant positions.
Projected ongoing vacancies of critical finance positions necessitate the continued use of Goldman & Wolfe, LLC. resources from May 18, 2026 through September 25, 2026, estimated at $168,700, which may also be funded by projected payroll savings achieved through vacant positions.
This amendment to the existing Agreement retroactive to September 15, 2025 is needed to increase the “not to exceed amount” from $197,600 to $580,000 in order to cover the additional $213,700 of costs already incurred since September 15, 2025 through May 18, 2026, and to cover the additional $168,700 of cost projected to be incurred from May 18, 2026 through September 25, 2026.

attachments.name: NS Second Reading Ord 26-07- Smoking and Vaping Prohibition  (1)
Rev. Business Impact Statement- Smoking and Vaping Prohibition Ord. 26-07

description:
Florida Statutes, Section 386.209, preempted local governments from regulating smoking in public buildings. In 2022, the law was amended to permit counties and municipalities to further “restrict smoking within the boundaries of any public beaches and public parks that they own, except that they may not further restrict the smoking of unfiltered cigars. A municipality may further restrict smoking within the boundaries of public beaches and public parks that are within its jurisdiction, but are owned by the county, unless such restriction conflicts with a county ordinance, except that they may not further restrict the smoking of unfiltered cigars.” The law as amended also allowed municipalities and counties to regulate the use of vapor-generating devices. Lee County recently adopted Ordinance 25-14 to prohibit smoking and vaping in county parks. The proposed ordinance amends the Town's current ordinance in accordance with Section 386.209 and regulates smoking and vaping in public parks and beaches, including county parks located within the territorial boundaries of the Town of Fort Myers Beach. It does not conflict with Lee County Ordinance 25-14 or restrict or regulate the use of unfiltered cigars.
A smoking ordinance is rarely mandatory, but can serve as:
A. A policy strength
Shows proactive governance and alignment with modern public-space standards.
B. A tie-breaker
When proposals are otherwise equal, communities with:
• Environmental protections
• Health policies
• Clean-beach initiatives
may score higher.
C. Supporting documentation
Can be cited in grant narratives under:
• Sustainability
• Public health commitment
• Environmental stewardship
• Visitor experience enhancement
________________________________________
Situations Where It Could Matter More for Fort Myers Beach
Given Fort Myers Beach’s profile as a tourism-driven coastal community, smoke-free policies may strengthen:
• Beach renourishment or coastal management narratives
• Blue Flag–style environmental certifications
• Marine debris reduction initiatives
• Eco-tourism branding
• Family-friendly destination marketing
• Post-hurricane “build back cleaner and safer” initiatives
________________________________________
Strategic Consideration
If the Town ever considered such a policy, it could be framed as:
“A public health, environmental protection, and visitor-experience measure aligned with coastal sustainability and family-friendly tourism goals.”
The draft ordinance was reviewed by the Town Council at their Management and Planning Meeting on March 5, 2026 with direction to Town staff to schedule the draft ordinance for first reading. At first reading April 6, 2026, questions were asked regarding whether enforcement of non-filtered and herbal cigarettes could also be excluded similar to non-filtered cigars. The regulation of smoking is pre-empted to the state. The Florida Legislature exercised its authority to exclude non-filtered cigars from the authority granted to local government. Legally, a municipality cannot create additional exclusions from regulation related to subjects that are pre-empted to state regulation.
Crescent Beach Park was also added to the ordinance as a county park located within the Town.
Staff was directed to post signs regarding the prohibition and to provide educational materials to the public. Sample signs observed in Pinellas County are attached for informational purposes only.

description:
The Town of Fort Myers Beach entered into grant agreement #32104 with the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) on March 25, 2025, and amended to extend the agreement period to end on July 31 2026. The purpose of Florida’s Urban and Community Forestry Capacity (UCF-C) grant program is to provide financial assistance to local governments, to initiate or enhance local urban and community forestry programs; and improve the urban environment within the State of Florida.
The grant funded work to be conducted includes procurement and installation of 74 native canopy trees and palms in Town beach accesses, right of ways, Newton Park, Bay Oaks Recreational Park, and FMB Elementary School Campus. The object is to restore canopy.and beautify Fort Myers Beach after the devastation caused by Hurricane Ian. All trees will be planted with organic fertilizer (e.g. black cow) and irrigated with tree watering bags to provide regular irrigation throughout the grow in period of 60 days. Tree health will be assessed at 60 days, 6 months, and 1 year for foliage, growth and signs of disease. A report will be compiled with geolocated photos of each tree and notes on the growth and health of each tree.

description:
The purpose of the Beach Management Program is to restore the Town's critically eroding beach, utilizing high quality beach compatible sand to provide erosion control and storm damage reduction along approximately 6.5 miles of critically eroding gulf shoreline along Estero Island, Lee County. In addition, beach nourishment provides environmental protection and enhancement for threatened and endangered species, including shorebirds and sea turtles, through creation and maintenance of habitats, monitoring, and implementation of the best management practices and safeguards during construction.
The Project has been in effect for several years. In December 2011, Lee County completed construction of the Estero Island Beach Restoration Project, including sand placement along the north segment of the island and the addition of a terminal groin on the northern end of the beach fill. The initial 2011 beach restoration project was constructed between April 2011 and December 2011. Approximately 403,000 cubic yards (CY) of sand were excavated and placed in the beach fill area between Bowditch Point (C-174A.5) and Crescent Park (R-181.5) The beach was constructed to a berm height of 2.9 feet NAVD88 over a shoreline distance of approximately 6,700 feet (1.3 miles). All dredging was conducted in the Matanzas Pass Ebb Shoal Borrow Area located in the Gulf of Mexico approximately 1.4 miles southwest of the Project area. In addition, a terminal groin was constructed at Bowditch Point with approximately 3,630 tons of limestone rock for a length of 240 feet with a maximum crest width of approximately 12.7 feet.
In 2020, the Town of Fort Myers Beach took over the local sponsorship for beach renourishment projects from the County. The Town contracted with Coastal Engineering Consultants to conduct a project performance assessment (CEC, 2020). The initial project was proposed to renourish the previously constructed North Segment between Bowditch Point (C-174A.5) and Crescent Park (R-181.5), plus the Central Segment from Margaritaville Resort (R-182) to Lanark St (R-198). The additional Central Segment was initially included in the County's 2011 project, but was dropped due to lack of beachfront property owner participation.
In 2020 and 2021, the Island was impacted by multiple tropical storms and hurricanes, most notably Tropical Storm Eta (2020) and Hurricane Elsa (2021). Multiple beachfront property owners located primarily in the south segment, which has never been restored, requested the Town include them in their beach management program.In response, the Town expanded the Project to include the southern shoreline segment between Creciente Condo (~ R-203) and Sun Caper Condo (~ R-207).
In 2022, Hurricane Ian devastated Fort Myers Beach and eroded approximately 220,000 cubic yards of sand from the beaches of Estero Island. The Town applied to FEMA for Category B public assistance to build a berm on the "natural beach" from Margaritaville Resort (R-182) to Island's End Condo (R-210). In addition, the Town applied for Category G public assistance to replace the 56,845 CY of sand eroded from the North Segment. The Category G public assistance was added to the scope of the Estero Island Beach Nourishment Project, adding Hurricane Recovery to the Project.
Both State and Federal Permitting applications were pending prior to Hurricane Ian. In early 2023, the Florida Department of Environmental Protection issued a Joint Coastal Permit and Submerged Lands Authorization, which expires in January 2038. The permit was modified to authorize a one-time placement of approximately 15,000 cubic yards of beach compatible material above Mean High Water (MHW) on the southern end of Estero Island (R209 to R-210) to offset the observed storm loss in this section of the island, which has not been restored previously. In addition, a second offshore burrow area was added to the project scope to provide ample sand resources for future renourishment projects. The US Army Corps Permit providing Federal authorization for the Estero Island Beach Nourishment and Hurricane Recovery Project was issued November 15, 2023.
The Estero Island Beach Nourishment and Hurricane Recovery Project mobilized in July 2024. The contractor, Ahtna Marine and Construction Company, LLC (Ahtna) placed approximately 927,448 cubic yards (total volume) on Estero Island. Based on the pre- and post-construction surveys, approximately 935,435 cubic yards were excavated from the Nearshore Borrow Area (NBA), which is now exhausted. All work including final site clean-up and demobilization was completed on September 9, 2025.
The purpose of the currently purposed Estero Island Dune Repair and Scour Fill Truck Haul Project is to restore dune elevations and address underfilled areas left behind by the previous dredge contractor. Sand will be truck-hauled and placed in low-elevation areas to reduce future pooling.

On February 25, 2026, the bid for the Estero Island Dune Repair and Scour Fill Truck Haul Project iwas issued. Seven responses were received and reviewed by the Town's consultant. The consultant recommended acceptance of the response from Earth Tech Enterprises, Inc. as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder. An intent to award the bid to Earth Tech Enterprises, Inc.was issued on April XX, 2026 and the matter was placed on the Town Council agenda for April 20, 2026 for award.

The town reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive minor irregularities in an otherwise valid bid. A minor irregularity is a variation from the bid invitation that does not affect the price of the bid, or give the bidder an advantage or benefit not enjoyed by the other bidders, or does not adversely impact the interests of the Town.

Sec. 34-112. - Purpose and Scope.
The broad objectives of town planning and the creation of the local planning agency are to further the welfare of the citizens of the town by helping to promote a better, more helpful, convenient, efficient, healthful, safe, and attractive community environment and to insure that the unique and natural characteristics of the island are preserved.
Sec. 34-113. - Composition, appointment and compensation of members.(a)The local planning agency shall consist of up to seven members appointed by the town council. No members of the local planning agency shall be salaried officials of the town. Membership on the local planning agency shall not affect a person's eligibility for membership on any other advisory committee for the Town of Fort Myers Beach during his/her term of office. One spouse per household will be eligible for membership on the local planning agency during any given term of office. No current member of town council shall be eligible to serve on the local planning agency. Except for inclusion of members required under Florida law, all members must be registered voters within the territorial boundaries of the Town of Fort Myers Beach at the time of application for membership on the local planning agency and during the period of service on the local planning agency. All applicants must apply on or before October 1 of the appointment year. Each application must include a short biography and short explanation as to why the applicant wishes to serve on the local planning agency.
(b)The members of the local planning agency shall serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for expenses as are necessary to conduct the work of the agency from funds appropriated by the town council.
(c)In addition to the up to seven voting members, the local planning agency shall also include as a nonvoting member a representative of the Lee County School District, as designated by the Lee County School Board, to attend and participate in those meetings at which the local planning agency considers comprehensive plan amendments and rezonings that would, if approved, increase residential density on the property that is the subject of the application (see F.S. 163.3174(1), 2002).
(d)All appointed members of the local planning agency must file an annual financial disclosure as required by the Florida Commission on Ethics.

description:
Florida Statutes, Section 386.209, preempted local governments from regulating smoking in public buildings. In 2022, the law was amended to permit counties and municipalities to further “restrict smoking within the boundaries of any public beaches and public parks that they own, except that they may not further restrict the smoking of unfiltered cigars. A municipality may further restrict smoking within the boundaries of public beaches and public parks that are within its jurisdiction, but are owned by the county, unless such restriction conflicts with a county ordinance, except that they may not further restrict the smoking of unfiltered cigars.” The law as amended also allowed municipalities and counties to regulate the use of vapor-generating devices. Lee County recently adopted Ordinance 25-14 to prohibit smoking and vaping in county parks. The proposed ordinance amends the Town's current ordinance in accordance with Section 386.209 and regulates smoking and vaping in public parks and beaches, including Bowditch Park, Lynn Hall Memorial Park, and the pier which are county parks located within the territorial boundaries of the Town of Fort Myers Beach. It does not conflict with Lee County Ordinance 25-14 or restrict or regulate the use of unfiltered cigars.
A smoking ordinance is rarely mandatory, but can serve as:
A. A policy strength
Shows proactive governance and alignment with modern public-space standards.
B. A tie-breaker
When proposals are otherwise equal, communities with:
• Environmental protections
• Health policies
• Clean-beach initiatives
may score higher.
C. Supporting documentation
Can be cited in grant narratives under:
• Sustainability
• Public health commitment
• Environmental stewardship
• Visitor experience enhancement
________________________________________
Situations Where It Could Matter More for Fort Myers Beach
Given Fort Myers Beach’s profile as a tourism-driven coastal community, smoke-free policies may strengthen:
• Beach renourishment or coastal management narratives
• Blue Flag–style environmental certifications
• Marine debris reduction initiatives
• Eco-tourism branding
• Family-friendly destination marketing
• Post-hurricane “build back cleaner and safer” initiatives
________________________________________
Strategic Consideration
If the Town ever considered such a policy, it could be framed as:
“A public health, environmental protection, and visitor-experience measure aligned with coastal sustainability and family-friendly tourism goals.”

description:
The Town's Dune Management Plan (DMP) is authorized by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) permit number #0413684-001-JC. This permit is issued under the authority of Chapter 161, which includes consideration of the provisions contained in Part IV of Chapter 373, Florida Statutes (F.S.), and Title 62, Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.). Pursuant to Operating Agreements executed between the Department of Environmental Protection (Department) and the water management districts, as referenced in Chapter 62-113, F.A.C., the Department is responsible for reviewing and taking final agency action on this activity.
The long-term success of the Town's Dune Management Plan is dependent on the continuity of each Managed Beach Zone (MBZ), and the collective efforts of the program. In order for staff and partnering agencies to monitor the long-term progress of the program and for the Town to have a reasonable assurance of success after commitment of funds; it is essential to have a pledge from each property owner to maintain the planting in at least a minimum condition. If a property owner wishes to be able to control the nature and height of vegetation and/or the height of dunes, as described in the plan, the property owner will be required to enter into a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the Town for their MBZ and adhere to the program parameters. The MOA process is described in the Town's DMP as follows:
Each MOA will be kept on file at the Town to effect compliance with the timelines, terms, and conditions of the program for current and future property owners. Each MOA will contain at a minimum:
Property owner name, address, STRAP, number, and signature,
Aerial photograph (available from www.leepa.org at no charge), plat, or survey of the property,
Scaled diagram of the area to be planted and including pedestrian walkthroughs or dune walkovers (Town staff can assist by utilizing GPS mapping),
Plant selection including species, sizes, and quantities,
Layout and design of any proposed rope and bollard systems,
Location of any proposed temporary irrigation,
If, at any time the Town inspections reveal that the MBZ is found to be non-compliant with the MOA, then the property owner may be required to bring the MBZ into compliance or reimburse the Town for the cost of the materials and/or installation.

John Prinz, on behalf of Gordian Multistrategy Fund LLC, the owner of the property located at 173 Gulf Island Drive, is requesting a variance from the Town of Fort Myers Beach Land Development Code (LDC) Section 34-638(d)(6)b.3. This section requires single-family residences and all attached accessory structures, including decks and staircases, within the Single-Family Residential (RS) zoning district to maintain a minimum twenty-foot (20’) side street setback for lots greater than seventy-five (75) feet in width.
The subject property is a corner lot developed with a single-family residence constructed in 1996. The existing residence has a nonconforming front street setback of 24.19 feet along Gulf Island Drive and a nonconforming side street setback of 8.1 feet along Bayside Road. The residence also includes an existing thirty-six (36) square-foot deck along Gulf Island Drive, which has a nonconforming side street setback of 17.57 feet.
The applicant proposes to expand the existing deck to a total of two hundred thirty-two (232) square feet and is requesting a variance of 11.9 feet to allow a side street setback of 8.1 feet for the expanded deck, where a minimum twenty-foot (20’) side street setback is otherwise required for lots greater than seventy-five (75) feet in width within the RS zoning district.
During the LPA hearing on January 13, the LPA voted 7-0 to recommend denial of the variance request from LDC section 34-638(d)(6)b.3., a request to reduce the required 20-foot side street setback by 11.9 feet to allow a 232-square-foot deck for the existing single-family residence in the RS zoning district. The LPA unanimously recommended denial, finding that the request does not meet the requirements of LDC Section 34-87, and that granting the variance would be injurious to the neighborhood or otherwise detrimental to the public welfare.

description:
Michael Martell, the applicant for 166/168 Coconut Drive, is requesting a Special Exception to increase the number of bedrooms as part of a redevelopment utilizing the Post-Disaster Buildback policy. Based on data available from the Lee County Property Appraiser’s Office, the structure supported a duplex, or two-family residence, with a total of five (5) bedrooms and three (3) bathrooms prior to Hurricane Ian.
The Town’s Buildback policy allows an applicant, by right, to increase the number of full bathrooms to equal the number of bedrooms that existed in the structure prior to a storm. Any additional bedrooms or bathrooms must be requested through the Special Exception process. The applicant is now proposing six (6) bedrooms and five (5) full bathrooms and is requesting a Special Exception for the additional bedroom.
The homeowner has stated that he intends to live in one of the dwelling units and rent the other dwelling unit, as permitted within his zoning district. Based on supporting data submitted by the applicant, staff confirmed that the structure was eligible to be rebuilt with two (2) living units pursuant to the Post-Disaster Buildback provisions.
The property is a nonconforming lot within the Single-Family Residential (RS) zoning district. Prior to Hurricane Ian, the primary structure was nonconforming due to a staircase encroaching into the required twenty-five-foot (25’) street setback and the required seven-and-one-half-foot (7.5’) side setback along the west side of the property. The applicant plans to replace the staircase in the same location and will apply for a variance prior to the issuance of building permits.
The Town’s LPA reviewed the application on January 13, 2026, and unanimously voted to recommend approval with conditions for Town Council’s consideration.

description:
The Town's current procurement policies were last updated in 2024 through Ordinance 24-11. The Town has undergone many changes including continuing recovery efforts with Hurricane Ian and staff believe it is in the best interest of the Town and public to update these policies.
Since the 2024 revision, the Town has received feedback from various agencies such as the Florida Division of Emergency Management, on ways that the procurement procedures could be updated to follow ongoing best practices.
Also, as part of the participation in the Florida Division of Emergency Management's F-ROC (Florida Recovery Obligation Calculation) program, the Town received customized abatement recommendations to strengthen our debris and emergency protective measures. This updated policy helps to address these recommendations to increase the Town's preparedness and potential to receive more future funding upfront through a higher score for expenses related to Category A (Debris Removal) and Category B (Emergency Protective Measures).
The draft ordinance aims to address clarification of existing procedures, further define procedures for services, incorporate grant and federal funding requirements for applicable purchases, and to implement revisions based on recommendations from the Town's Disaster Readiness Assessment.

description: Florida Statutes, Section 386.209, preempted local governments from regulating smoking in public buildings. In 2022, the law was amended to permit counties and municipalities to further “restrict smoking within the boundaries of any public beaches and public parks that they own, except that they may not further restrict the smoking of unfiltered cigars. A municipality may further restrict smoking within the boundaries of public beaches and public parks that are within its jurisdiction, but are owned by the county, unless such restriction conflicts with a county ordinance, except that they may not further restrict the smoking of unfiltered cigars.” The law as amended also allowed municipalities and counties to regulate the use of vapor-generating devices. Lee County recently adopted Ordinance 25-14 to prohibit smoking and vaping in county parks. The proposed ordinance amends the Town's current ordinance in accordance with Section 386.209 and regulates smoking and vaping in public parks and beaches, including Bowditch Park, Lynn Hall Memorial Park, and the pier which are county parks located within the territorial boundaries of the Town of Fort Myers Beach. It does not conflict with Lee County Ordinance 25-14 or restrict or regulate the use of unfiltered cigars. ; and

description:
From the Request for Qualifications: The Town of Fort Myers Beach (the "Town") seeks qualifications from professional Landscape Architecture and design firms to provide comprehensive design, permitting, and construction-phase engineering and inspection (CEI) services for the Parks and Recreation Revitalization Project. This project, funded in part through Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) funds, aims to restore, improve, and modernize public recreation facilities that were severely impacted by Hurricane Ian. The firm selected will provide professional services for the Redevelopment of the Newton Park Beach Facility.
The successful firm must have experience in post-disaster infrastructure restoration, flood mitigation planning, resilient and sustainable design, and compliance with federal procurement and CDBG-DR regulations.
Through this solicitation, the Town seeks an experienced, engineering, and design firm to provide comprehensive professional services that align with FEMA flood mitigation guidelines, CDBG-DR program requirements, and sustainable development best practices. The project will not only restore these vital community assets but also integrate resilient infrastructure solutions to protect against future climate-related threats.
Pursuant to Sec. 2-480(h)(1) of the Town's Code of Ordinances and the Consultant's Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA), contracts for professional services consisting of Architecture, Professional Engineering, Landscape Architecture or Registered Land Surveying must be competitively negotiated in accordance with the requirements of Section 287.055 F.S. within statutory thresholds. In addition, the Town competitively bids for other professional services as further described below.
The Town re-solicited this project under RFQ-25-17-AD, with responses due in October 2025 and the Town receiving four responses from Chen Moore and Associates, EnSite, Inc., Kimley-Horn and Associates ​Inc., and JR Evans Engineering P.A..
In accordance with the Town of Fort Myers Beach Purchasing Ordinance 24-11, Sec 2-480 (14) the Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) consisting of a minimum of three members, may be established for the purpose of evaluating bids submitted to the Town. All members of the SAC are prohibited from speaking, answering questions or having contact with any potential bidder. The SAC will review the bid and response materials prior to the SAC meeting. The committee evaluates each firm's qualifications based on past experience, express understanding of the project and proposed method of handling the project and any other criteria included for evaluation.
The Town's SAC, consisting of the Deputy Town Manager, Community Services Director, and Community Development Director, was established for the purpose of evaluating the Request for Qualifications proposals received by the Town, and met on the 13th day of November 2025 to evaluate each firm's qualifications. At the noticed public meeting, the firms were publicly evaluated based upon the established criteria within the Request for Qualifications document, and the SAC short-listed three firms were then invited for a public interview and discussion, which occurred on February 11, 2026, in which the Selection Advisory Committee announced and deemed an ordered list of JR Evans Engineering P.A., Kimley-Horn and Associates, and Chen Moore and Associates to be the most responsive and qualified to perform the required services after their evaluation as a recommendation to the Town Manager. The SAC also held a meeting on December 18th to clarify the interview process in preparation of their interview meeting.
The Town Manager, after reviewing the SAC recommendation, has forwarded this to the Town Council for consideration during a regularly scheduled meeting. The Town Council is requested to review the rankings and qualifications of the firms and vote to accept, reject or modify the rankings by the Town Manager. The Town Council is requested to also direct the Town Manager or designee to initiate negotiations with the top ranked firm if authorized.

description:
Following the Town’s ongoing recovery efforts, a substantial amount of material was generated through various reconstruction and infrastructure projects. To reduce expenses and improve operational efficiency, the Town elected to keep this material on the island rather than haul it offsite. This choice resulted in meaningful cost savings and supported a streamlined workflow for crews working throughout the community.
As work progressed, the volume of dirt delivered to the temporary staging area at 2525 Estero Blvd exceeded initial projections. The growing stockpile created several operational and safety concerns. Excess runoff from the mounds posed a risk of clogging nearby stormwater drains, which could lead to localized flooding and require costly cleaning and restoration of the stormwater system. In addition, the height and accessibility of the dirt piles created liability issues, as members of the public could easily access the material, increasing the potential for injuries and related legal claims.
Town staff evaluated multiple options for addressing these concerns. Initially, the proposed solution—to repurpose the material and construct a parking lot—was well within the Town Manager’s purchasing authority, and staff obtained three competitive quotes in accordance with procurement requirements. This approach provided a cost‑effective way to eliminate the risks posed by the dirt piles while creating needed parking for residents, visitors, and the local workforce.
However, as the design evolved, it became clear that a retaining wall would be required to stabilize the site, enhance safety, and properly manage stormwater runoff. The addition of this structural component increased the overall project scope and cost beyond the Town Manager’s purchasing authority. Accordingly, Town Council approval is now required to move forward with construction of the parking lot and the associated retaining wall due to unanticipated conditions, allowing for the waiving of the competitive bid requirements in the Town's procurement code.

description: The Aries Voyager stormwater video system van allows us to capture video evidence of the structural integrity of the entire stormwater system. It allows the utilities department to improve the effectiveness of system improvements, repairs, and maintenance to achieve maximum stormwater management. This also aligns with the first thing the Federal Emergency Management Association (FEMA) asks for after an event, which is video evidence of the system before the storm and then evidence after the storm. This will increase our ability to get the maximum amount of funding available. description:
The Town contracted Ahtna Marine and Construction Company, LLC (AMCC) to construct the Estero Island Beach Renourishment and Hurricane Recovery Project. AMCC mobilized to the work site beginning in July 2024. Sand placement began on the North Beach segment (R-176 to R-182) on August 10, 2024 and pumping was completed on December 20, 2024. Sand placement began on the Central Beach segment (R-182 to R-198) and was paused in January 2025 as Ahtna moved to the South Beach segment (R-203 to R-207) and began pumping sand. Ahtna completed South Beach on May 14, 2025 then returned to Central Beach and restarted pumping. Ahtna competed Central Beach on August 22, 2025. All work including final site clean-up and demobilization was completed on September 9, 2025.

Central Beach: Ahtna excavated and placed 299,922 cubic yards (pay volume) within the permitted fill template between R-181.7 and R-198. Ahtna placed approximately 324,374 cubic yards of sand (total volume) on Central Beach.
South Beach: Ahtna placed 297,701 cubic yards (pay and total volume) within the permitted fill template between R-203 and R-207. Of this volume, approximately 32,000 cubic yards were transported and placed from Stewart Materials’ inland mines.
Total: Ahtna placed approximately 927,448 cubic yards (total volume) on Estero Island.

description:
John Prinz, on behalf of Gordian Multistrategy Fund LLC, the owner of the property located at 173 Gulf Island Drive, is requesting a variance from the Town of Fort Myers Beach Land Development Code (LDC) Section 34-638(d)(6)b.3. This section requires single-family residences and all attached accessory structures, including decks and staircases, within the Single-Family Residential (RS) zoning district to maintain a minimum twenty-foot (20’) side street setback for lots greater than seventy-five (75) feet in width.
The subject property is a corner lot developed with a single-family residence constructed in 1996. The existing residence has a nonconforming front street setback of 24.19 feet along Gulf Island Drive and a nonconforming side street setback of 8.1 feet along Bayside Road. The residence also includes an existing thirty-six (36) square-foot deck along Gulf Island Drive, which has a nonconforming side street setback of 17.57 feet.
The applicant proposes to expand the existing deck to a total of two hundred thirty-two (232) square feet and is requesting a variance of 11.9 feet to allow a side street setback of 8.1 feet for the expanded deck, where a minimum twenty-foot (20’) side street setback is otherwise required for lots greater than seventy-five (75) feet in width within the RS zoning district.
During the LPA hearing on January 13, the LPA voted 7-0 to recommend denial of the variance request from LDC section 34-638(d)(6)b.3., a request to reduce the required 20-foot side street setback by 11.9 feet to allow a 232-square-foot deck for the existing single-family residence in the RS zoning district. The LPA unanimously recommended denial, finding that the request does not meet the requirements of LDC Section 34-87, and that granting the variance would be injurious to the neighborhood or otherwise detrimental to the public welfare.

description:
Michael Martell, the applicant for 166/168 Coconut Drive, is requesting a Special Exception to increase the number of bedrooms as part of a redevelopment utilizing the Post-Disaster Buildback policy. Based on data available from the Lee County Property Appraiser’s Office, the structure supported a duplex, or two-family residence, with a total of five (5) bedrooms and three (3) bathrooms prior to Hurricane Ian.
The Town’s Buildback policy allows an applicant, by right, to increase the number of full bathrooms to equal the number of bedrooms that existed in the structure prior to a storm. Any additional bedrooms or bathrooms must be requested through the Special Exception process. The applicant is now proposing six (6) bedrooms and five (5) full bathrooms and is requesting a Special Exception for the additional bedroom.
The homeowner has stated that he intends to live in one of the dwelling units and rent the other dwelling unit, as permitted within his zoning district. Based on supporting data submitted by the applicant, staff confirmed that the structure was eligible to be rebuilt with two (2) living units pursuant to the Post-Disaster Buildback provisions.
The property is a nonconforming lot within the Single Family Residential (RS) zoning district. Prior to Hurricane Ian, the primary structure was nonconforming due to a staircase encroaching into the required twenty-five-foot (25’) street setback and the required seven-and-one-half-foot (7.5’) side setback along the west side of the property. The applicant plans to replace the staircase in the same location and will apply for a variance prior to the issuance of building permits.
The Town’s LPA reviewed the application on January 13, 2026, and unanimously voted to recommend approval with conditions for Town Council’s consideration.

description:
James Ink of Ink Engineering, Inc., representing the applicant, is requesting rezoning of the property located at 175 Sterling Avenue from Institutional to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) for the redevelopment of the Fort Myers Beach Woman’s Club.
The subject property at 175 Sterling Avenue housed the Fort Myers Beach Woman's Club in a building constructed in 1947 and occupied beginning in 1950. The current zoning of the property is Institutional, and the future land use category is Boulevard. The property is located at the rear end of the Boulevard and runs parallel to Estero Boulevard, making it suitable for rezoning to CPD without requiring a comprehensive plan amendment.
On December 16, 2025, the Local Planning Agency (LPA) voted unanimously (6–0) to recommend approval with conditions for CPD Amendment Request No. 20250203, which proposes rezoning the subject property from Institutional to Commercial Planned Development for the redevelopment of the Fort Myers Beach Woman's Club.
On January 20, 2026, Town Council heard CPD Request No. 20250203 to rezone the subject property from Institutional to Commercial Planned Development for the redevelopment of the Fort Myers Beach Woman's Club. The Council voted unanimously, identifying two major items to be addressed prior to the second reading:
1. Reconsideration of the COP area to include the entire property as a COP permit area.
2. Addition of conditions or language in the approval requiring the use of the property to remain for a non-profit activities.

description:
From the Request for Qualifications: The Town of Fort Myers Beach (the "Town") seeks qualifications from professional engineering and design firms to provide comprehensive design, permitting, and construction-phase engineering and inspection (CEI) services for the Parks and Recreation Revitalization Project. This project, funded in part through Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) funds, aims to restore, improve, and modernize public recreation facilities that were severely impacted by Hurricane Ian. The selected firm will provide professional services as described for The Bay Oaks Community Pool Rehabilitation Project. The successful firm must have experience in post-disaster infrastructure restoration, flood mitigation planning, resilient and sustainable design, and compliance with federal procurement and CDBG-DR regulations. Through this solicitation, the Town seeks an , engineering, and design firm to provide comprehensive professional services that align with FEMA flood mitigation guidelines, CDBG-DR program requirements, and sustainable development best practices. The project will not only restore these vital community assets but also integrate resilient infrastructure solutions to protect against future climate-related threats.
Pursuant to Sec. 2-480(h)(1) of the Town's Code of Ordinances and the Consultant's Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA), contracts for professional services consisting of Architecture, Professional Engineering, Landscape Architecture or Registered Land Surveying must be competitively negotiated in accordance with the requirements of Section 287.055 F.S. within statutory thresholds. In addition, the Town competitively bids for other professional services as further described below.
On October 6, 2025, the Town Council rejected and canceled the previous RFQ-25-10-AD qualification proposal for the Fort Myers Beach Engineering & Architectural Services Bay Oaks Community Pool Rehabilitation Project with cause, due to lack of adequate competition as provided in the Request for Qualifications and Sections 2-480(i)(12) and 2-480(h)(5)(e) of the Town Code, and provide direction to staff to re-bid the project and the Town re-solicitied as RFQ-26-02-AD, with responses due in November 2025.
In accordance with the Town of Fort Myers Beach Purchasing Ordinance 24-11, Sec 2-480 (14) the Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) consisting of a minimum of three members, may be established for the purpose of evaluating bids submitted to the Town. All members of the SAC are prohibited from speaking, answering questions or having contact with any potential bidder. The SAC will review the bid and response materials prior to the SAC meeting. The committee evaluates each firm's qualifications based on past experience, express understanding of the project and proposed method of handling the project and any other criteria included for evaluation.
The Town's SAC, consisting of the Deputy Town Manager, Community Services Director, and Community Development Director, was established for the purpose of evaluating the Request for Qualifications proposals received by the Town, and met on the 9th day of December 2025 to evaluate each firm's qualifications. At the noticed public meeting, the firm was evaluated based upon the established criteria within the Request for Qualifications document. The firm was then invited for a public interview and discussion, which occurred on January 9, 2026 in which the SAC announced and deemed the response to be the most highly responsive and qualified to perform the required services. The Town Manager, after reviewing the SAC recommendation, has forwarded this to the Town Council for consideration during a regularly scheduled meeting. The Town Council is requested to review the rankings and qualifications of the firm and vote to accept, reject or modify the ranking by the Town Manager. description:
From the Request for Qualifications: The Town of Fort Myers Beach, Florida, is seeking Statements of Qualifications (SOQs) from Florida-licensed professional engineering firms to provide engineering, design, permitting, and construction oversight services for the rehabilitation of the North Island Water Tower Complex. This project is funded through the Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Critical Infrastructure Program, administered by Lee County.
Engineering services procured under this RFQ must adhere to 2 CFR 200.317-327, Florida Statutes, and all applicable federal, state, and local regulations.The North Island Water Tower Complex was severely damaged by Hurricane Ian, leaving the Town dependent on a single remaining potable water tank. This project is a critical infrastructure initiative to ensure resilient, secure, and sustainable potable water access for residents and businesses in Fort Myers Beach.
Through this solicitation, the Town seeks an experienced, engineering, and design firm to provide comprehensive professional services that align with FEMA flood mitigation guidelines, CDBG-DR program requirements, and sustainable development best practices. The project will not only restore these vital community assets but also integrate resilient infrastructure solutions to protect against future climate-related threats.
Pursuant to Sec. 2-480(h)(1) of the Town's Code of Ordinances and the Consultant's Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA), contracts for professional services consisting of Architecture, Professional Engineering, Landscape Architecture or Registered Land Surveying must be competitively negotiated in accordance with the requirements of Section 287.055 F.S. within statutory thresholds. In addition, the Town competitively bids for other professional services as further described below.
The Town re-solicited this project under RFQ-26-03-AD, with responses due in November 2025 and the Town receiving two responses from Dunham Engineering and Tetra Tech.
In accordance with the Town of Fort Myers Beach Purchasing Ordinance 24-11, Sec 2-480 (14) the Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) consisting of a minimum of three members, may be established for the purpose of evaluating bids submitted to the Town. All members of the SAC are prohibited from speaking, answering questions or having contact with any potential bidder. The SAC will review the bid and response materials prior to the SAC meeting. The committee evaluates each firm's qualifications based on past experience, express understanding of the project and proposed method of handling the project and any other criteria included for evaluation.
The Town's SAC, consisting of the Deputy Town Manager, Community Services Director, and Community Development Director, was established for the purpose of evaluating the Request for Qualifications proposals received by the Town, and met on the 9th day of December 2025 to evaluate each firm's qualifications. At the noticed public meeting, the firms were publicly evaluated based upon the established criteria within the Request for Qualifications document, and the two firms were then invited for a public interview and discussion, which occurred on January 12, 2026 in which the Selection Advisory Committee announced and deemed an ordered list of Tetra Tech Inc. and then Dunham Engineering to be the most responsive and qualified to perform the required services after their evaluation as a recommendation to the Town Manager.
The Town Manager, after reviewing the SAC recommendation, has forwarded this to the Town Council for consideration during a regularly scheduled meeting. The Town Council is requested to review the rankings and qualifications of the firms and vote to accept, reject or modify the rankings by the Town Manager. The Town Council is requested to also direct the Town Manager or designee to initiate negotiations with the top ranked firm if authorized.

description: The Aries Voyager stormwater video system van allows us to capture video evidence of the structural integrity of the entire stormwater system. It will show where tidal or groundwater infiltration may be occurring, collapsed piping, junction degradation, blockages, and provide for integration of our system into our GIS program. It allows the utilities department to improve the effectiveness of system improvements, repairs, and maintenance to achieve maximum stormwater management. This also aligns with the first thing the Federal Emergency Management Association (FEMA) asks for after an event, which is video evidence of the system before the storm and then evidence after the storm. This will increase our ability to get the maximum amount of funding available. In addition, according to our Sotuh Florida Water Management District (SFWMD), Individual Environmental Resource Permit No. 36-102467-P, “The operation and maintenance entity must perform periodic inspections to identify if there are any deficiencies in structural integrity, degradation due to insufficient maintenance, or improper operation of projects that may endanger public health, safety, or welfare, of the water resources.” Being able to do this in-house will save us significant financial expenses. During emergencies, we would not have to rely on other people.
