description: This Second Amendment of resolution 25-235 meter replacement program is to allow the National Metering Service to gather geospatial position system (GPS) location data and make a service line identification inventory of all meters in our distribution system. The GPS data provides for a sub-meter accurate location of all the water meters in our system using GPS longitude and latitude data. This data is used to quickly and accurately locate our meters for regular system maintenance. In addition, during emergency situations, we will be able to identify the meters for quick shut-offs, preventing us from shutting off entire mains because the meter is buried under debris, sand, or other situations that happen during emergency events. This will save work hours (cost), possible damage to peoples' homes or businesses from massive leaks, and lost revenue from uncontrollable breaks. The service line identification inventory is to identify lead and or copper service lines either before or after the meter. Through the identification, we can schedule the replacement of those service lines before the meters and inform the residents of the lines that are after the meter. This action brings our system into compliance with Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Rule 62-555.350(14) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), administered by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP), Rule 40 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Section 141.80-91,That state we must maintain an accurate and updated map of our distribution system which includes the lead and copper service line inventory. Combining this data with our cellular metering installation, valve exercising data, stormwater voyage video van data and our GIS program, we are on the cutting edge of technology and are a leader in the industry.

description:
The Town entered into a loan agreement on May 3, 2021 with the Florida Water Pollution Control Financing Corporation under the State Revolving Fund to finance stormwater improvements project SW360860 for an initial loan amount of $12,500.000.00.
The Town authorized amendment #1 to the Loan Agreement on February 16, 2022 with the Florida Water Pollution Control Financing Corporation for an additional loan amount of $3,704,800.00, bringing the total loan amount to $16,204,800.00.
The Town authorized amendment #2 to the Loan Agreement on August 1, 2023 with the Florida Water Pollution Control Financing Corporation to reschedule the start of the loan repayment from April 2023 to April 2025 as a result of the impact of Hurricane Ian.
The Town authorized amendment #3 to the Loan Agreement on February 6, 2024 with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection to transfer oversight and management from the Florida Water Pollution Control Financing Corporation to the Florida Department of Environmental Protection.
The Town authorized amendment #4 to the Loan Agreement on June 12, 2024 with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection under the State Revolving Fund to provide for advance payments to the Town, allowing the Town to request reimbursement for expenditures in advance of actual payment by the Town.
The Town intends to continue to construct necessary improvements to its stormwater system and desires to borrow an additional $8,265,117.00 from the State Revolving Fund to finance those improvements, bringing the total loan amount to $24,469,917.00.

description: Pursuant to a competitive procurement process in compliance with state law and Town Code – RFP-23-03-UT “Stormwater Maintenance and Repair” - in February of 2023 the Town and the (“Firm”), entered into a Service Provider Agreement for Stormwater Maintenance and Repair (“Agreement”). The agreement included a provision for additional services. In June of 2024, the Town was overwhelmed by utility locate requests as a result of two factors: the loss of personnel who were experienced at performing utility locates which resulted in an extended staffing shortage in the Water Department, and an increased demand for utility locates resulting from underground utility installation as well as the FP&L lighting project. As a result, the Town entered into an agreement with Earthview to provide utility locate services as additional services provided under their contract. Since the total amount of the services are approaching the $75,000 threshold that requires Town Council approval, and since the need for utility locate services from Earthview is expected to continue until it reaches as much as $130,000 by June 2025, the town is bringing this resolution to Town Council to approve a not-to-exceed amount of $130,000 retroactive to June 2024.

description:
This case, Leo J. DiBiasi, Trustee of the Leo J. Dibiasi and Valerie J. DiBiasi Revocable Living Trust v. Town of Fort Myers Beach (Fla. 20th Judicial Circuit 23-CA-005377), involved the Town’s removal of a ramp and construction of drainage infrastructure on the DiBiasi property. On December 4, 2024, a mediation was held between the parties. Chris Stearns, Esquire represented the Town on behalf of the Town’s liability carrier. Town Manager Andrew Hyatt and Town Attorney Nancy Stuparich also participated in the mediation.
The Town Council tentatively agreed to a settlement, subject to final approval of a settlement agreement to be approved by the Town Council, of payment in the amount of $85,000 in exchange for an easement to allow the Town’s drainage infrastructure to remain in its present location. The settlement agreement formalizes this prior approval and provides greater detail regarding the implementation of its terms. A copy of the settlement agreement will be provided prior to or at the February 3, 2025 public meeting for final approval.

description:
Per the Town Charter:
Sec. 4.02. Mayor.
At the first meeting after the second Tuesday in November, the council, by majority vote, shall elect from its membership a mayor. The mayor shall serve as chairperson during meetings of the council and shall serve as the head of municipal government for the purpose of execution of legal documents as required by ordinance. The mayor shall also serve as the ceremonial head of the town.
Sec.4.03. Vice mayor.
At the first meeting after the second Tuesday in November, the council, by a majority vote, shall elect from among its membership a vice mayor who shall serve as mayor during the absence or disability of the mayor and, if a vacancy occurs, shall become interim mayor pursuant to section 4.08 of this charter.

Application Pkg - Hideaway Village CPD Rezone

description:
The Neighborhood Company, on behalf of SLASA LLC, is requesting rezoning of the property located at 5601 and 5607 Estero Boulevard from the Commercial Resort (CR) zoning district to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) for redevelopment of the historic Hideaway Village Motel. The subject property is located on the northeast side of Estero Boulevard at Lazy Way and Lewis Street. The property consists of approximately 0.63 acres and is identified as STRAP(s) #33-46-24-W2-00204.0290 and 33-46-24-W2-00001.0120. Before Hurricane Ian, the property contained the Hideaway Village Motel, a three-building, two-story lodging development with 23 total units, including 22 guest units, together with a swimming pool, outdoor dining areas, and on-site and off-site parking.The applicant proposes a CPD rezoning to allow redevelopment of the site with a 30-unit boutique hotel and complementary restaurant, café/coffee shop, limited accessory retail, and hotel amenities.
The proposed Master Concept Plan includes 30 lodging units, up to 3,500 square feet of restaurant and commercial space, and a minimum of 36 parking spaces.
The Master Concept Plan relocates most parking beneath or behind the principal structure, eliminates direct vehicular access and backing movements onto Estero Boulevard, provides ingress from Lazy Way and egress to Lewis Street, adds a sidewalk along Lazy Way, and incorporates enhanced landscaping and pedestrian amenities along Estero Boulevard and Lazy Way. Five parking spaces are proposed within the Lewis Street right-of-way and would require separate authorization under the Town’s private use-of-right-of-way process.
On September 8, 2026, the LPA voted unanimously (6-0) to recommend approval, with conditions, of CPD amendment request CPD 20260039, which includes nine deviations, to rezone the property from Commercial Resort (CR) to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) to redevelop Hideaway Village with 30 boutique hotel units and 3,500 square feet of commercial space.
On October 5, 2026, the Town Council voted unanimously to recommend approval, with conditions, of CPD amendment request CPD 20260039, which includes nine deviations, to rezone the property from Commercial Resort (CR) to Commercial Planned Development (CPD) to redevelop Hideaway Village with 30 boutique hotel units and 3,500 square feet of commercial space.

description:
Mark Raudenbush of Idyll Construction Inc., authorized agent for property owner Linda LaMere, sole owner of Beach House 41734, LLC, requests approval to rezone approximately 0.295 acres from Residential Conservation (RC) to Residential Planned Development (RPD); reconstruct two duplex buildings containing four dwelling units; approve a Master Concept Plan, Schedule of Uses, and three deviations; and approve a maximum of 12 bedrooms and eight full bathrooms.
The subject property is located at the corner of Estero Boulevard and Matanzas Street. The approximately 0.295-acre property contains 12,861 square feet and is irregularly shaped. Based on the submitted survey, the property meets the applicable minimum lot area, width, and depth requirements of the RC zoning district. According to Lee County Property Appraiser records, residential buildings have existed on the property since the 1980s. Before Hurricane Ian, the property contained two elevated residential buildings. Both buildings were destroyed and have since been removed. Based on records provided by the applicant and the Lee County Property Appraiser, Building 1 had an approximately 1,326-square-foot roof footprint and two stories, resulting in approximately 2,652 square feet under roof. Building 2 had an approximately 1,708-square-foot roof footprint and two stories, resulting in approximately 3,416 square feet under roof.
The Lee County Property Appraiser's records identify five pre-disaster dwelling units: two units in Building 1 at 681 Estero Boulevard and three units in Building 2 at 683 Estero Boulevard. Historical rental documentation also references Units A through E. The proposed development would contain two duplex buildings with four dwelling units, one fewer than the five dwelling units documented before Hurricane Ian. The pre-disaster development contained 10 bedrooms and six full bathrooms. The proposed development would contain 12 bedrooms and eight full bathrooms. Accordingly, the applicant requests approval of the proposed bedroom and bathroom counts pursuant to LDC Section 34-3238(2)e.4.a. as part of the RPD public-hearing process.
The applicant requests the RPD rezoning because the proposed redevelopment does not meet all requirements of the existing RC zoning district. The applicant proposes to use the RM zoning district regulations as the base standards for the RPD and construct two duplex buildings containing four dwelling units. The project would be constructed in two phases. Phase 1 would include Building 1 and its associated driveway at 681 Estero Boulevard, on the beach side of the property. Phase 2 would include Building 2 and its associated driveway at 683 Estero Boulevard, on the bay side of the property, restoration of the pool, and completion of the final landscaping.

description:
Estero Island Beach Club Association, Inc. is requesting a special exception to redevelop an approximately 8,834-square-foot pool and amenity area within the Environmentally Critical zoning district between the 1978 Lee County Coastal Construction Control Line and the existing seawall.
The subject property is located on the Gulf side of Estero Boulevard, approximately one-half mile southeast of Times Square. Estero Island Beach Club was established in approximately 1981 through the conversion of a hotel into a 75-unit time-share resort. Before Hurricane Ian, the property contained two resort buildings, a pool, an amenity deck, and a seawall seaward of the 1978 Coastal Construction Control Line. Hurricane Ian substantially damaged the property. The resort buildings were subsequently demolished, and the damaged amenity decking was removed. The existing pool and seawall remain.
On June 16, 2025, the Town Council adopted Ordinance 25-13, rezoning the landward portion of the property from Downtown to Commercial Planned Development to allow redevelopment of the 75-unit timeshare resort and associated facilities. Ordinance 25-13 approved a Master Concept Plan, Schedule of Uses, four deviations, and conditions of approval. The area seaward of the 1978 Coastal Construction Control Line was not included within the Commercial Planned Development and remains within the Environmentally Critical zoning district.
The current application is therefore limited to the approximately 8,834-square-foot area within the Environmentally Critical zoning district between the 1978 Coastal Construction Control Line and the existing seawall. Approval of this special exception would not modify Ordinance 25-13, its approved Master Concept Plan, Schedule of Uses, deviations, or conditions of approval. Historical aerial photographs submitted by the applicant show that a pool and amenity deck occupied this general location before Hurricane Ian. However, the proposed development is not a strict like-for-like replacement. The applicant proposes a redesigned amenity area containing pavers, artificial turf, a 90-square-foot pervious planter area, an additional 1,491-square-foot area of impervious artificial turf or pavers, two chickee huts, two grill stations, the refurbished existing pool, open space, and two existing beach-access gates. In 2021, Estero Island Beach Club applied for a permit for a chickee hut under Permit Number 210356. The permit was rejected because special-exception approval was required for the proposed structure within the Environmentally Critical zoning district. Accordingly, the current application should not be characterized as reconstruction of a previously approved chickee hut. The two proposed chickee huts are new components of the redesigned amenity area and are included in this special-exception request.

description:
Over the past year, staff have received several inquiries from the condo association regarding the 75-percent requirement in Section 34-201(a)(1). The condo association and time-share association have been unable to collect signatures from 75 percent of unit owners to initiate a public hearing.
Section 34-201(a)(1) governs who may initiate applications requiring a public hearing. Subsection (b) currently requires a condominium or time-share owners’ association and at least 75 percent of unit owners to jointly initiate an application. Subsection (c) requires at least 75 percent of subdivision lot or parcel owners and the homeowners’ association, if applicable, to initiate an application.
The regulation in Section 34-201(a)(1) is based on Section 718.113(2), Florida Statutes. Section 718.113(2), Florida Statutes, establishes an approval procedure for certain material alterations or substantial additions to condominium common elements or association property. When the declaration does not specify an approval procedure, the statute may require approval by 75 percent of the applicable voting interests before the work begins. It does not establish a general requirement that 75 percent of unit owners join in filing a Town land use application. The proposed amendment removes the Town’s filing threshold; it does not change approvals required by state law or condominium governing documents.
Proposed Solution
Staff proposes the following strike-through and underline changes to remove the 75-percent filing requirement for the public hearing process. A condominium or time-share owners’ association could initiate an application without obtaining signatures from 75 percent of owners solely for filing with the Town. For subdivisions, an applicable homeowners’ association or the owners of the lots or parcels subject to the application could initiate the application. The existing provisions regarding owner lists, notice, and attorney opinions would remain unchanged.
LPA Motion
On October 13, 2026, the LPA voted unanimously (7-0) to recommend the text amendment regarding the 75-percent requirement in Section 34-201(a)(1) of the Land Development Code.

description:
SB 1134 has now been enacted as Chapter 2026-43, Laws of Florida, and will take effect on January 1, 2027. It creates Section 166.04971, Florida Statutes, applicable to municipalities, as well as a new contracting certification requirement in Section 287.139.
Under this new law, beginning January 1, 2027, the Town may not directly or indirectly fund or promote DEI, take official action relating to DEI, operate or staff a DEI office, engage a DEI officer, or authorize Town funds to be used by employees, contractors, volunteers, vendors, or agents to promote DEI initiatives. Existing Town ordinances, resolutions, rules, regulations, programs, or policies falling within the statutory prohibition will be void. The new law also provides "[a]ny member of the governing body of a municipality or other municipal official acting in an official capacity who violates this section commits misfeasance or malfeasance in office." The ordinance's intent and policy is to mandate compliance with the new law and create a continuing obligation on the part of the Town to remain in compliance with the new law's requirements.

description:
The Town of Fort Myers Beach completed a yearlong process to develop a vision for the Town and a strategic plan to help make that vision a reality. Throughout the project, the research team engaged stakeholders and gathered feedback through a variety of opportunities designed to inform and shape the final plan.
Residents, business owners, and community stakeholders played an important role in developing a shared vision in partnership with the Town. Their active participation and valuable input helped chart a course for the Town’s future success, resilience, and harmonious growth. Community feedback collected throughout the process directly influenced the content and priorities of the final strategic plan.
The project concluded in 2026 with the delivery of a formal strategic plan document and presentation to the Town Council.
The Town of Fort Myers Beach engaged the USF Florida Institute of Government and SPC Collaborative Labs to facilitate the process. The Town extends its appreciation to all residents, business owners, and stakeholders who contributed their time, ideas, and feedback throughout this important community initiative.
The Town's Strategic Plan website can be accessed here, and the Final Report here.

description:
In accordance with Town Council Policies and Procedures, Council reorganization takes place at the first meeting after the second Tuesday in November. The reorganization may include designating a liaison to the Town's advisory committees. Whenever Town Council is called upon to make committee determinations, the Council should confirm its desire to continue its current committee structure.
The scope of each committee is listed as follows:
Anchorage Advisory Committee. Current liaison: John McLean
Advises Town Council and staff on all issues pertaining to the Town's public mooring field.
Audit Committee. Current liaison: Scott Safford
To serve in an advisory capacity to the Town Council in the election of an auditor to conduct the Town's annual financial audit and for other purposes as directed by Town Council.
Bay Oaks Recreational Campus Advisory Board. Current liaison: Rebecca Link
To serve the Town as a community center and recreational facility, providing individuals with social and community activities and events for both residents and visitors.
Cultural and Environmental Learning Center Advisory Board. Current liaison: John McLean
Oversees the Mound House and Newton Park; the goals are to manage and promote the cultural, historical and environmental resources of Fort Myers Beach.
Marine & Environmental Resources Task Force. Current liaison: John R. King
To promote stewardship of our marine resources, to stop further damage and to rehabilitate Estero Bay and its surrounding waters, wildlife, plant life and air/water quality.
Public Safety Committee. Current liaison: Dan Allers
To address any safety and transportation issues specifically assigned to the committee by the Town Council for the purpose of the health, safety and welfare of the citizens and visitors to the Town.

description:

A partnership of citizens and elected officials, and resource managers working together to protect and restore water and wildlife habitat in Central and Southwest Florida. The Policy Committee establishes the general policy for the CHNEP, has authority over program administration, appoints members to other committees and approves the CHNEP's budget. Meets January 26, 2023, May 25, 2023 and September 21, 2023. Current representation : John R. King, alternate TBD.

A Lee County government committee that advises the BoCC, staff and various related advisory boards when proceeding with a project affecting beach and shoreline preservation regarding the proper methods of helping to conserve the beaches of Lee County. Meets periodically throughout the year, usually on the 4th Monday; current representation: Town Environmental Projects Manager Chadd Chustz, alternate TBD.

Current representation: Dan Allers

description: Section 166.241, Florida Statutes, requires the Town of Fort Myers Beach to maintain a balanced budget for each fund and allows a municipality up to 60 days after the end of the fiscal year to amend the prior year’s budget. The FY2026 Adopted Budget included a transfer of $581,380 ($48,448.33 per month) from the General Fund to the General Debt Service Fund. In May 2024, the Town drew additional loan funds, which increased the annual payment to $581,468.40 ($48,455.70 per month). This increase was not reflected in the FY2026 Budget. This amendment adjusts the General Fund and the General Debt Service Fund by $88.40 (rounded to $89) to bring the FY2026 Budget into compliance with Florida Statutes.

description: At the Town of Fort Myers Beach, Town Council Meeting on August. 3, 2026 the Mayor informed the Town Council that representatives from Jarabacoa, a city in the Dominican Republic, contacted the Town to see if the Town would be interested in becoming its Sister City. The Town Attorney was asked to review whether there are any statutory requirements that would prevent the Town from doing so in view of recent statutory changes in Section 288.860(2), Florida Statutes.
title: A RESOLUTION OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF FORT MYERS BEACH, FLORIDA, AUTHORIZING THE TOWN MANAGER TO NEGOTIATE A SISTER CITY AGREEMENT WITH JARABACOA, DOMINICAN REPUBLIC SETTING FORTH THE PURPOSE, DUTIES, RESPONSIBILITIES, AND COMMITMENTS OF BOTH ENTITIES TO BE SUBSEQUENTLY REVIEWED FOR APPROVAL BY THE TOWN COUNCIL; AND PROVIDING FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE.
